words.enDefinition: involving competition or competitiveness

examples.en: Our quote is still competitive even after the freight costs went up last month.
examples.zh: 即使上个月运费涨了，我们的报价仍然「有竞争力」。

examples.en: Training twice a month keeps our service team competitive with the big chains.
examples.zh: 每月两次的培训让我们的服务团队和大连锁比依然「有竞争力」。

words.enDefinition: the state of being rich and affluent; having a plentiful supply of material goods and money

examples.en: He built his wealth slowly, buying small workshops before the district became popular.
examples.zh: 他慢慢积累「财富」，在这个城区走红之前买下了几家小作坊。

examples.en: The report shows that most household wealth in the region is tied up in property.
examples.zh: 报告显示，该地区大多数家庭的「财富」都沉淀在房产上。

words.enDefinition: very unusual or remarkable; going far beyond what is ordinary

examples.en: The sales team delivered an extraordinary result, tripling revenue in a single quarter.
examples.zh: 销售团队交出了「非凡的」业绩，一个季度就让收入翻了三倍。

examples.en: It takes extraordinary patience to keep a small family firm alive for forty years.
examples.zh: 让一家小家族企业撑过四十年，需要「非凡的」耐心。

words.enDefinition: administer or bestow, as in small portions

examples.en: The manager plans to distribute the bonus equally among everyone who worked on the launch.
examples.zh: 经理打算把奖金平均「分配」给参与新品发布的每位员工。

examples.en: Please distribute these catalogues to the shops that ordered samples last week.
examples.zh: 请把这些产品目录「分发」给上周订购样品的那几家商店。

words.enDefinition: not yet paid, resolved, or settled

examples.en: Two invoices remain outstanding from March, so please chase the buyer before Friday.
examples.zh: 还有两张三月份的发票「未付」，请在周五之前向买方催收。

examples.en: The supplier paused deliveries because our account still has an outstanding balance.
examples.zh: 由于我们账户上还有「未结清的」余款，供应商暂停了发货。

words.enDefinition: conforming exactly or almost exactly to fact or to a standard or performing with total accuracy

examples.en: Make sure the stock count is accurate before we place the order with the factory.
examples.zh: 向工厂下订单之前，务必确保库存盘点数字「准确」。

examples.en: Her forecast for holiday sales proved accurate within a few hundred pounds.
examples.zh: 她对节日销量的预测相当「准确」，误差只有几百英镑。

words.enDefinition: daily written record of (usually personal) experiences and observations

examples.en: I keep a business diary to note supplier prices after every trade fair.
examples.zh: 我记一本生意「日记簿」，每次参展后把供应商的报价记下来。

examples.en: Check the diary on my desk; all of tomorrow's client meetings are written there.
examples.zh: 看一下我桌上的「日程簿」，明天所有的客户会面都记在上面。

words.enDefinition: request (spoken or written) to participate or be present or take part in something

examples.en: We mailed an invitation to every wholesaler on the list for the opening ceremony.
examples.zh: 我们给名单上的每家批发商都寄去了开业典礼的「邀请函」。

examples.en: She accepted the invitation to speak at the trade conference in Singapore.
examples.zh: 她接受了在新加坡贸易会议上发言的「邀请」。

words.enDefinition: compelling immediate action

examples.en: The client marked the repair order urgent, so we moved it to the front of the queue.
examples.zh: 客户把维修单标为「紧急」，我们把它排到了队伍最前面。

examples.en: It is urgent that we confirm the shipping date before the harbour closes for the holidays.
examples.zh: 港口放假封关之前必须确认船期，这件事十分「紧急」。

words.enDefinition: fractional monetary unit of Ireland and the United Kingdom; equal to one hundredth of a pound

examples.en: The shopkeeper rounded the bill down to the nearest penny to keep the customer happy.
examples.zh: 店主把账单抹零到最接近的「便士」，好让顾客满意。

examples.en: Costs rose by pennies per unit, yet across ten thousand units that mattered.
examples.zh: 单件成本只涨了几「便士」，可一万个加起来就不是小数目了。

words.enDefinition: the activities involved in promoting, selling, and distributing a product or service

examples.en: Good marketing made the little bakery famous across the whole city within a year.
examples.zh: 出色的「市场营销」让这家小面包店一年之内全城闻名。

examples.en: Our marketing budget is small, so we rely on social media and word of mouth.
examples.zh: 我们的「营销」预算不多，所以主要靠社交媒体和口碑。

words.enDefinition: everything a person owns, including all assets and liabilities; land and buildings owned

examples.en: She manages an estate of rented shops and flats near the old harbour.
examples.zh: 她管理着老港区一片由出租商铺和公寓组成的「房地产」。

examples.en: After grandfather died, the family estate was divided between the three children.
examples.zh: 祖父去世后，家里的「财产」由三个子女平分。

words.enDefinition: consider in detail and subject to an analysis in order to discover essential features or meaning

examples.en: Before we sign anything, I want our lawyer to analyse the contract clause by clause.
examples.zh: 签字之前，我要请律师逐条「分析」这份合同。

examples.en: The intern was asked to analyse last quarter's sales data for the Monday meeting.
examples.zh: 实习生被要求为周一的会议「分析」上一季度的销售数据。

words.enDefinition: the act of having and controlling property

examples.en: The lease ends on Friday, when the landlord will take possession of the whole shop.
examples.zh: 租约周五到期，届时房东将收回店铺的「占有权」。

examples.en: The police found stolen watches in his possession during a routine check.
examples.zh: 例行检查时，警察发现他「持有」失窃的手表。

words.enDefinition: an upper limit on prices, wages, or other quantities

examples.en: The board set a ceiling on travel expenses at two hundred pounds per trip.
examples.zh: 董事会给差旅费设了「上限」，每次不得超过两百英镑。

examples.en: Rent controls placed a ceiling on what landlords in the district may charge.
examples.zh: 租金管制给该地区房东的收费设了「上限」。

words.enDefinition: the payment of a debt or fulfilment of an obligation

examples.en: The bank accepted the land deed as satisfaction of the company's old debt.
examples.zh: 银行接受地契作为该公司旧债的「清偿」。

examples.en: Full satisfaction of the claim was recorded once the final payment cleared.
examples.zh: 最后一笔款项到账后，这笔索赔即告全额「清偿」并记录在案。

words.enDefinition: not engaged in a gainful occupation

examples.en: After the factory closed, nearly a third of the town was unemployed for months.
examples.zh: 工厂倒闭后，镇上近三分之一的人「失业」了好几个月。

examples.en: He had been unemployed since January, sending out CVs every single morning.
examples.zh: 他从一月起一直「失业」，每天早上都在投简历。

words.enDefinition: a flaw or disadvantage; the state of lacking strength

examples.en: Relying on one supplier is the biggest weakness in our whole supply chain.
examples.zh: 依赖单一供应商是我们整条供应链最大的「弱点」。

examples.en: Her weakness for agreeing to every discount hurt the shop's margins badly.
examples.zh: 她总是随口答应打折，这个「弱点」严重侵蚀了店铺利润。

words.enDefinition: volatile flammable mixture of hydrocarbons (hexane and heptane and octane etc.) derived from petroleum; used mainly as a fuel in internal-combustion engines

examples.en: The delivery van stopped for petrol on the way to the warehouse this morning.
examples.zh: 今天早上送货车在去仓库的路上停下加了「汽油」。

examples.en: Petrol prices jumped again, so the couriers started planning shorter routes.
examples.zh: 「汽油」价格又涨了，快递员们开始规划更短的路线。

words.enDefinition: well grounded in logic or truth or having legal force

examples.en: Your parking permit is valid until the end of March, so no renewal is needed yet.
examples.zh: 你的停车许可证三月底前仍然「有效」，暂时不用续办。

examples.en: The contract is only valid if both partners sign it before the deadline.
examples.zh: 只有双方合伙人在期限前签署，合同才「有效」。

words.enDefinition: having or showing or requiring special skill

examples.en: Skilled carpenters are hard to find, so we pay apprentices while they train.
examples.zh: 「熟练的」木工很难找，所以学徒培训期间我们也发工资。

examples.en: The factory needs skilled workers to run the new cutting machines safely.
examples.zh: 工厂需要「技术熟练的」工人来安全操作新的切割机。

words.enDefinition: the creation of something in the mind

examples.en: The young engineer patented his invention before showing it at the trade fair.
examples.zh: 年轻工程师在商展会展示之前，先为自己的「发明」申请了专利。

examples.en: Every great invention in shipping, from containers to GPS, changed freight costs.
examples.zh: 航运业的每一项伟大「发明」，从集装箱到卫星定位，都改变了货运成本。

words.enDefinition: the state of being unemployed or not having a job

examples.en: Unemployment in the shipyard towns doubled after the orders from abroad stopped.
examples.zh: 国外订单中断后，造船城镇的「失业率」翻了一番。

examples.en: The government promised new training schemes to fight youth unemployment.
examples.zh: 政府承诺推出新的培训计划来应对年轻人「失业」问题。

words.enDefinition: a person who is travelling or who travels often, especially for work

examples.en: Every traveller entering the country must declare goods worth more than the limit.
examples.zh: 每位入境「旅客」都必须申报超过限额的物品。

examples.en: The hotel offers business travellers a free shuttle to the exhibition centre.
examples.zh: 酒店为商务「旅客」提供前往会展中心的免费班车。

words.enDefinition: preparatory school work done outside school (especially at home)

examples.en: The trainer asked the whole sales team to do some homework on the client before the pitch.
examples.zh: 培训师让整个销售团队在提案前先做「功课」，研究一下客户。

examples.en: My daughter finishes her homework at the kitchen table while I answer emails.
examples.zh: 女儿在餐桌旁写「家庭作业」，我则在一旁回复邮件。

words.enDefinition: personal belongings packed for travel; luggage

examples.en: The airline lost two bags of trade-sample baggage on the Frankfurt flight.
examples.zh: 航空公司把两袋装着贸易样品的「行李」弄丢在了法兰克福航班上。

examples.en: Allow extra time at the airport to collect your baggage before the meeting.
examples.zh: 开会前取「行李」，要在机场多留出一些时间。

words.enDefinition: transactions (sales and purchases) having the objective of supplying commodities (goods and services)

examples.en: The new port brought commerce back to a town that factories had left behind.
examples.zh: 新港口让这座被工厂抛弃的城镇恢复了「商业」生机。

examples.en: E-commerce now makes up a fifth of our clothing business.
examples.zh: 电子「商务」如今占到了我们服装业务的五分之一。

words.enDefinition: the part played by a person in bringing about a result

examples.en: Her contribution to the product launch was praised at the year-end meeting.
examples.zh: 她在产品发布会上的「贡献」在年终会议上受到了表扬。

examples.en: Every employee makes a small monthly contribution to the office coffee fund.
examples.zh: 每位员工每月向办公室咖啡基金交一小笔「捐款」。

words.enDefinition: (of quantities) imprecise but fairly close to correct

examples.en: The renovation will take approximately eight weeks, so we can reopen in May.
examples.zh: 装修「大约」需要八周时间，所以我们五月份能重新开业。

examples.en: Approximately two hundred guests are expected at the supplier's anniversary dinner.
examples.zh: 供应商的周年晚宴预计有「大约」两百位宾客出席。

words.enDefinition: a request for information or for prices and details about goods

examples.en: We received an enquiry from a German buyer asking for our winter price list.
examples.zh: 我们收到一位德国买家的「询价」，想要我们的冬季报价单。

examples.en: For any enquiry about your order, please quote the number on the invoice.
examples.zh: 如对订单有任何「疑问」，请提供发票上的编号。

words.enDefinition: the ability to make sensible decisions; an opinion formed after thinking carefully

examples.en: In a fast market, a buyer's judgement about timing matters more than any formula.
examples.zh: 在瞬息万变的市场里，买家的「判断」比任何公式都重要。

examples.en: The manager showed poor judgement by promising delivery dates we could not meet.
examples.zh: 经理承诺了我们根本做不到的交期，可见他的「判断力」很差。

words.enDefinition: the act of departing

examples.en: The departure of the cargo ship was delayed again by the storm warnings.
examples.zh: 风暴警报再度推迟了货轮的「启运」。

examples.en: Please confirm the departure time of the train carrying the samples to Leeds.
examples.zh: 请确认运送样品去利兹那班火车的「发车」时间。

words.enDefinition: suddenly and by a large amount; in a severe or critical way

examples.en: Cotton prices fell sharply after the harvest came in three weeks early.
examples.zh: 棉花提前三周收成后，价格「急剧」下跌。

examples.en: The director spoke sharply to the team about missing the shipping deadline.
examples.zh: 主管就错过发货期限一事「严厉地」批评了团队。

words.enDefinition: the procedure of calculating; determining something by mathematical or logical methods

examples.en: One small error in the tax calculation cost the firm a penalty notice.
examples.zh: 税务「计算」里的一处小错让公司吃了一张罚单。

examples.en: Let me double-check the calculation before we quote a price to the buyer.
examples.zh: 给买家报价之前，我再核对一遍「计算」结果。

words.enDefinition: once every year; yearly

examples.en: The insurance premium is reviewed annually, usually in the first week of January.
examples.zh: 保险费「每年」复核一次，通常在一月的第一个星期。

examples.en: The firm awards its best supplier annually at the spring trade dinner.
examples.zh: 公司「每年」在春季贸易晚宴上表彰最佳供应商。

words.enDefinition: public or private structure (business or governmental or educational) including buildings and equipment for business or residence

examples.en: The bakery is the oldest food establishment still trading in the old quarter.
examples.zh: 这家面包店是老城区仍在营业的最老一家「企业」。

examples.en: Opening a new establishment abroad costs more than the founders expected.
examples.zh: 在国外开设新的「经营场所」比创始人预想的要贵。

words.enDefinition: member of the Democratic Party

examples.en: The senator, a lifelong democrat, pushed the small-business tax relief through Congress.
examples.zh: 这位一辈子都是「民主党人」的参议员，推动小企业减税法案获得了国会通过。

examples.en: As a democrat, she argued that public contracts should favour local workers.
examples.zh: 作为「民主党人」，她主张公共合同应向当地工人倾斜。

words.enDefinition: written agreement between two states or sovereigns

examples.en: The two governments signed a trade treaty that cuts tariffs on machinery.
examples.zh: 两国政府签署了一项削减机械关税的贸易「条约」。

examples.en: Fishing rights were settled in a treaty signed between the coastal states.
examples.zh: 沿海各国通过一项「条约」解决了捕捞权问题。

words.enDefinition: firm engaged in trading

examples.en: Our dealer in Geneva can source vintage watches at auction within a week.
examples.zh: 我们日内瓦的「经销商」能在一周内通过拍卖弄到古董手表。

examples.en: The bond dealer called twice before noon to quote us today's rate.
examples.zh: 债券「交易员」中午前打来两次电话，报出今天的利率。

words.enDefinition: the branch of social science that deals with the production and distribution and consumption of goods and services and their management

examples.en: She studied economics at Manchester before joining her father's import firm.
examples.zh: 她在曼彻斯特攻读「经济学」，之后加入了父亲的进口公司。

examples.en: Basic economics explains why the price of strawberries falls in June.
examples.zh: 基础「经济学」解释了为什么六月草莓会降价。

words.enDefinition: someone who purchases and maintains an inventory of goods to be sold

examples.en: Our trader in Hong Kong buys silk outright and sells it to European mills.
examples.zh: 我们在香港的「贸易商」直接买入丝绸，再转卖给欧洲的织造厂。

examples.en: The coffee trader hedged next season's crop to protect against price falls.
examples.zh: 咖啡「商人」对下季收成做了对冲，以防价格下跌。

words.enDefinition: the right to use and enjoy property; pleasure derived from use

examples.en: The deed gives the family full enjoyment of the holiday cottage they rent out.
examples.zh: 契约让这家人对他们出租的度假小屋拥有完整的「使用权」。

examples.en: He took obvious enjoyment from fixing the old cash registers himself.
examples.zh: 他亲手修好旧收银机，显然「乐在其中」。

words.enDefinition: the act of moving something from one location to another

examples.en: Transportation costs doubled after the ferry company changed its fuel surcharge.
examples.zh: 轮渡公司调整燃油附加费后，「运输」成本翻了一倍。

examples.en: The farmer relies on rail transportation to get milk to the city by dawn.
examples.zh: 农场主靠铁路「运输」在天亮前把牛奶送进城。

words.enDefinition: (economics) the ratio of the quantity and quality of units produced to the labor per unit of time

examples.en: New packing machines lifted productivity on the bottling line by a fifth.
examples.zh: 新包装机让灌装线的「生产率」提高了五分之一。

examples.en: The manager blames long meetings for the drop in office productivity.
examples.zh: 经理把办公室「生产率」下降归咎于冗长的会议。

words.enDefinition: an extra sales commission paid to a manager or agent, often on sales made by others

examples.en: The regional manager earns an override on every sale her team closes.
examples.zh: 团队每做成一单生意，这位区域经理都能抽取「追加佣金」。

examples.en: Head office pays dealers an override commission on machines sold by sub-agents.
examples.zh: 总部按子代理售出的机器，向经销商支付「覆盖佣金」。

words.enDefinition: of or belonging to a corporation

examples.en: She left a corporate job in banking to run a small pottery studio.
examples.zh: 她辞去了银行里一份「公司」职位，去经营一家小陶艺工作室。

examples.en: The corporate headquarters moved to Leeds, leaving fifty staff in Manchester.
examples.zh: 「公司」总部迁到了利兹，五十名员工留在了曼彻斯特。

words.enDefinition: legal practitioner who advises clients and prepares cases; also a person who solicits contributions

examples.en: Our solicitor checked the lease carefully before we signed for the new shop.
examples.zh: 签下新店铺之前，我们的「律师」仔细核对了租约。

examples.en: The solicitor advised the charity on how to register the legacy properly.
examples.zh: 「律师」就如何规范登记这笔遗赠给慈善机构出了主意。

words.enDefinition: hypothesis that is taken for granted

examples.en: The whole budget rests on the assumption that fuel prices stay flat.
examples.zh: 整份预算都建立在油价保持平稳的「假定」之上。

examples.en: Your sales forecast is built on a risky assumption about holiday demand.
examples.zh: 你的销售预测建立在一个关于节日需求的冒险「假设」上。

words.enDefinition: general inclusive concept

examples.en: The interns struggled with the notion of negative equity at first.
examples.zh: 实习生们起初很难理解「负资产」这个概念。

examples.en: He dismissed the notion that customers would pay extra for faster delivery.
examples.zh: 他不同意顾客愿意为更快配送多付钱这种「想法」。

words.enDefinition: person who buys

examples.en: The buyer from the department store wants samples by the end of the week.
examples.zh: 百货公司的「买手」要求周末前收到样品。

examples.en: A serious buyer inspected the warehouse and asked about the lease terms.
examples.zh: 一位认真的「买家」查看了仓库，并询问租约条款。

words.enDefinition: following in time or order

examples.en: The initial shipment arrived late, and all subsequent orders were cancelled.
examples.zh: 首批货物迟到，「随后的」所有订单都被取消了。

examples.en: In subsequent meetings, the client kept asking for extra features.
examples.zh: 在「后来的」几次会议上，客户不断要求增加额外功能。

words.enDefinition: the state of being combined into one body

examples.en: Three small farms formed a coalition to buy fertiliser at lower prices.
examples.zh: 三家小农场组成「联盟」，以便用更低价格购买化肥。

examples.en: A coalition of retailers asked the council to delay the parking charges.
examples.zh: 零售商「联盟」要求市政会推迟实施停车收费。

words.enDefinition: the people employed in an organisation; the department that manages staff records

examples.en: All warehouse personnel must attend the safety briefing on Monday morning.
examples.zh: 全体仓库「员工」都必须参加周一上午的安全简报。

examples.en: Personnel files for the branch staff are stored in the locked cabinet.
examples.zh: 分店员工的「人事」档案锁在柜子里保存。

words.enDefinition: including all or everything

examples.en: The consultant produced a comprehensive report on our logistics costs.
examples.zh: 顾问就我们的物流成本出具了一份「全面的」报告。

examples.en: The new insurance policy offers comprehensive cover for the delivery fleet.
examples.zh: 新保险单为送货车队提供「全面的」保障。

words.enDefinition: the act of contracting or assuming or acquiring possession of something

examples.en: The acquisition of the rival bakery doubled our share of the local market.
examples.zh: 对竞争对手面包店的「收购」使我们本地市场份额翻倍。

examples.en: Before the acquisition closes, auditors will check every asset on the balance sheet.
examples.zh: 「收购」交割前，审计师会核对资产负债表上的每一项资产。

words.enDefinition: the main activity a person does to earn money; a job

examples.en: Please state your occupation and employer on the credit application form.
examples.zh: 请在信用卡申请表上填写你的「职业」和雇主。

examples.en: Teaching used to be the most common occupation in her family.
examples.zh: 教书曾经是她家最普遍的「职业」。

words.enDefinition: the relation of an owner to the thing possessed; possession with the right to transfer possession to others

examples.en: Ownership of the trademark passes to the new company next month.
examples.zh: 商标的「所有权」将于下月移交新公司。

examples.en: The brothers argued about ownership of the workshop their father built.
examples.zh: 兄弟俩为父亲建造的作坊的「所有权」争执不休。

words.enDefinition: relating to or concerned with strategy

examples.en: Opening a warehouse near the port was a strategic decision for the exporter.
examples.zh: 在港口附近设仓是这家出口商的「战略性」决定。

examples.en: We cut two product lines as part of a strategic review of the business.
examples.zh: 作为业务「战略」评估的一部分，我们砍掉了两条产品线。

words.enDefinition: cloth made by weaving or knitting fibres

examples.en: The tailor imports linen fabric from small mills on the Irish coast.
examples.zh: 裁缝从爱尔兰海岸的小工厂进口亚麻「布料」。

examples.en: This waterproof fabric keeps the work jackets selling all winter.
examples.zh: 这种防水「面料」让工作夹克整个冬天都畅销。

words.enDefinition: an undivided or unbroken completeness or totality with nothing wanting

examples.en: The partners showed unity by backing the same price cut without argument.
examples.zh: 合伙人们毫无异议地支持同一轮降价，展现出「团结」。

examples.en: There is little unity between the sales office and the factory floor.
examples.zh: 销售办公室与车间之间缺乏「一致性」。

words.enDefinition: common to or shared by two or more parties

examples.en: The two firms signed the deal for mutual benefit, not out of friendship.
examples.zh: 这两家公司签约是为了「共同的」利益，而不是交情。

examples.en: After the dispute, both sides agreed to resume trade as a sign of mutual respect.
examples.zh: 争执过后，双方同意恢复贸易，以示「相互」尊重。

words.enDefinition: (usually plural) the office that serves as the administrative center of an enterprise

examples.en: The bank's headquarters in Frankfurt approved the loan within two days.
examples.zh: 银行位于法兰克福的「总部」两天内就批准了贷款。

examples.en: Staff at headquarters rarely see how deliveries actually reach rural shops.
examples.zh: 「总部」员工很少了解货物实际是怎么送到乡村商店的。

words.enDefinition: formal public statement

examples.en: The merger announcement lifted the share price by ten percent before lunch.
examples.zh: 合并「公告」发布后，股价在午前就上涨了百分之十。

examples.en: Staff heard about the closure through a company announcement, not from managers.
examples.zh: 员工是从公司「通告」而非经理口中得知关厂消息的。

words.enDefinition: fail to agree with; be in violation of; as of rules or patterns

examples.en: The factory was fined because it violated the new rules on waste water.
examples.zh: 这家工厂因「违反」废水新规而被罚款。

examples.en: Delivering late every month violates the terms of our supply agreement.
examples.zh: 月月延迟交货「违反」了我们供货协议的条款。

words.enDefinition: to carry out or complete an obligation or contract

examples.en: The workshop worked overnight to fulfil the wedding order on time.
examples.zh: 作坊连夜赶工，按时「完成」了那笔婚礼订单。

examples.en: We must fulfil our promise to deliver free samples to every new client.
examples.zh: 我们必须「履行」向每位新客户免费寄样的承诺。

words.enDefinition: marked by simplicity; having a humble opinion of yourself

examples.en: The firm grew at a modest pace, opening one shop a year at most.
examples.zh: 公司以「温和的」速度增长，至多一年开一家新店。

examples.en: He stayed modest about the award, crediting his whole team instead.
examples.zh: 他对获奖保持「谦虚」，把这归功于整个团队。

words.enDefinition: the act of formally leaving a job or position

examples.en: The finance director handed in her resignation a week after the audit.
examples.zh: 审计结束一周后，财务总监递交了「辞呈」。

examples.en: News of the manager's resignation spread through the office before noon.
examples.zh: 经理「辞职」的消息中午前就在办公室传开了。

words.enDefinition: laborer who works in a mine

examples.en: Every miner on the night shift must log the equipment checks before leaving.
examples.zh: 夜班每名「矿工」下班前都必须登记设备检查情况。

examples.en: His father was a miner in the valley before the colliery closed.
examples.zh: 在煤矿关闭前，他父亲是山谷里的一名「矿工」。

words.enDefinition: the combination of two or more commercial companies

examples.en: The merger of the two shipping firms created the largest fleet in the north.
examples.zh: 两家航运公司的「合并」造就了北方最大的船队。

examples.en: Regulators delayed the merger until they studied its effect on port fees.
examples.zh: 监管机构推迟了这项「并购」，先研究它对港口费的影响。

words.enDefinition: give an incentive for action

examples.en: Quarterly bonuses motivate the sales team far better than long speeches.
examples.zh: 季度奖金比长篇讲话更能「激励」销售团队。

examples.en: The supervisor motivates new staff by rotating them through every station.
examples.zh: 主管让新员工轮换每个工位，以此「激发」他们的积极性。

words.enDefinition: intentional deception resulting in injury to another person

examples.en: The accountant discovered fraud in the travel claims three months ago.
examples.zh: 会计三个月前发现了差旅报销中的「欺诈」行为。

examples.en: Selling counterfeit watches as genuine counts as fraud under trading law.
examples.zh: 把假手表当真品出售，按交易法构成「欺诈」。

words.enDefinition: person or thing having the same function or characteristics as another

examples.en: Our Paris counterpart handles all the French orders while we cover Spain.
examples.zh: 我们的巴黎「对口同事」负责全部法国订单，我们负责西班牙。

examples.en: The minister met her Chinese counterpart to discuss export licences.
examples.zh: 部长与中方「对等官员」会晤，讨论出口许可证事宜。

words.enDefinition: contract granting the right to operate a subsidiary business

examples.en: The city granted the company a concession to run the ferry service.
examples.zh: 市政府授予该公司经营轮渡服务的「特许权」。

examples.en: As a concession to the union, management agreed to review shift pay.
examples.zh: 作为对工会的「让步」，管理层同意审核轮班工资。

words.enDefinition: a group of people sent to represent others, especially at a meeting

examples.en: A trade delegation from Brazil visited our factory to discuss coffee imports.
examples.zh: 巴西贸易「代表团」参观了我们的工厂，洽谈咖啡进口。

examples.en: The sales director will lead the delegation at the expo in Osaka.
examples.zh: 销售总监将率「代表团」参加大阪的博览会。

words.enDefinition: grant paid by a government to an enterprise that benefits the public

examples.en: The farm received a government subsidy for keeping the hedgerows intact.
examples.zh: 农场因保留树篱而拿到了政府「补贴」。

examples.en: Without the heating subsidy, many small shops could not survive winter.
examples.zh: 没有取暖「补助金」，许多小商店撑不过冬天。

words.enDefinition: a person who buys and sells goods, securities, or insurance for others

examples.en: Our insurance broker compared twelve policies before the renewal date.
examples.zh: 续保日期前，我们的保险「经纪人」比较了十二份保单。

examples.en: The shipping broker found a return cargo so the vessel sails full both ways.
examples.zh: 船舶「经纪人」找到了回程货，船双向都能满载。

words.enDefinition: diplomatic building where ambassadors live or work

examples.en: The export paperwork was stamped at the embassy in Madrid on Tuesday.
examples.zh: 出口文件周二在马德里的「大使馆」盖了章。

examples.en: Travelling staff must register with the embassy before crossing the border.
examples.zh: 出差员工在过境前必须到「大使馆」登记。

words.enDefinition: yielding material gain or profit

examples.en: The catering van proved more profitable than the shop it replaced.
examples.zh: 事实证明，这辆餐车比它取代的店铺更「有利可图」。

examples.en: Selling refills keeps the ink business profitable between big orders.
examples.zh: 售卖补充装让墨水生意在大订单间隙依然「有利可图」。

words.enDefinition: to buy and sell goods, property, or shares hoping to profit from market changes

examples.en: Investors speculate in farmland when city property gets too expensive.
examples.zh: 当城市地产过热时，投资者便转向农田「投机」。

examples.en: He lost savings speculating on coffee futures during the price spike.
examples.zh: 咖啡价格飙升期间，他「投机」咖啡期货赔掉了积蓄。

words.enDefinition: man salesperson

examples.en: The furniture salesman demonstrated how the sofa folds into a bed.
examples.zh: 家具「销售员」演示了沙发如何折叠成床。

examples.en: A good salesman listens first and quotes a price only after that.
examples.zh: 优秀的「销售员」先倾听，然后才报价。

words.enDefinition: money paid out; an amount spent

examples.en: Capital expenditure on the new oven will pay for itself in two years.
examples.zh: 新烤炉的资本「支出」两年内就能收回。

examples.en: We track every expenditure over fifty pounds in the shared spreadsheet.
examples.zh: 超过五十英镑的每一笔「开支」我们都记录在共享表格里。

words.enDefinition: the state of being obligated to do or pay something

examples.en: Paying suppliers within thirty days is a contractual obligation, not a favour.
examples.zh: 三十天内付款是合同「义务」，不是人情。

examples.en: He felt an obligation to repay the loan even after the partnership ended.
examples.zh: 即使合伙关系结束，他也觉得自己有「义务」还清贷款。

words.enDefinition: person who makes things

examples.en: The soap maker supplies three hotels in the city with guest toiletries.
examples.zh: 这家肥皂「制造商」向城内三家酒店供应客房洗护用品。

examples.en: Every maker at the craft market must show liability insurance.
examples.zh: 手工市集上的每位「制作人」都必须出示责任保险。

words.zhGloss: 管理人员；行政管理人员
words.enDefinition: someone who administers a business
acceptedZhAnswers: 管理人员；行政管理人员

examples.en: The office administrator keeps the invoice files and books the meeting rooms.
examples.zh: 办公室「行政管理员」负责保管发票档案并预订会议室。

examples.en: A court appointed an administrator to run the factory until debts are settled.
examples.zh: 法院指定了一名「管理人」接管工厂，直至债务清偿完毕。

words.enDefinition: to control or adjust something by rules or by a device

examples.en: The agency regulates food imports to keep expired goods off the shelves.
examples.zh: 该机构对食品进口进行「监管」，防止过期商品上架。

examples.en: A small thermostat regulates the temperature inside the cheese storehouse.
examples.zh: 小恒温器「调节」着奶酪库房里的温度。

words.enDefinition: management by overseeing the performance or operation of a person or group

examples.en: New forklift drivers work under close supervision for their first month.
examples.zh: 新叉车司机上岗第一个月要在严格「监督」下工作。

examples.en: The auditor noted that cash handling lacks proper supervision on weekends.
examples.zh: 审计员指出，周末的现金管理缺乏适当的「监督」。

words.enDefinition: someone who organizes a business venture and assumes the risk for it

examples.en: The young entrepreneur turned a market stall into three bakeries in five years.
examples.zh: 这位年轻「企业家」五年内把一个市场摊位做成了三家面包店。

examples.en: As an entrepreneur, she risks her savings rather than borrow from the bank.
examples.zh: 作为「创业者」，她宁可押上积蓄也不向银行借钱。

words.enDefinition: a person who manages property or other affairs for someone else; an attendant on a ship or plane

examples.en: The family steward manages the estate accounts and deals with the tenants.
examples.zh: 家族的「管家」管理庄园账目，并与佃户打交道。

examples.en: A cabin steward showed the passengers where the life jackets were stored.
examples.zh: 客舱「乘务员」告诉乘客救生衣存放在哪里。

words.enDefinition: money or property donated to an institution; natural abilities or qualities

examples.en: The library survives on an endowment left by a shipping merchant in 1902.
examples.zh: 图书馆靠一位船商1902年留下的「捐赠基金」维持运转。

examples.en: Her endowment for languages showed when she picked up Portuguese in months.
examples.zh: 几个月就学会了葡萄牙语，可见她在语言上的「天分」。

words.enDefinition: make a subtraction

examples.en: The accountant will deduct the damaged goods from next month's invoice.
examples.zh: 会计会把损坏货物的货款从下月发票中「扣除」。

examples.en: Staff can deduct training fees from their taxable income this year.
examples.zh: 员工今年的培训费可以从应税收入中「扣减」。

words.enDefinition: to officially recognise that a person or organisation meets required standards

examples.en: The agency accredits laboratories that test drinking water for councils.
examples.zh: 该机构为替各市政会检测饮用水的实验室进行「认证」。

examples.en: The business school is accredited by two international auditing bodies.
examples.zh: 这所商学院获得了两家国际认证机构的「认可」。

words.enDefinition: very wealthy or powerful businessman

examples.en: The hotel tycoon started by buying one seaside guesthouse with borrowed money.
examples.zh: 这位酒店「大亨」最初靠借来的钱买下一家海边小旅馆起家。

examples.en: Newspapers described the shipping tycoon as the richest man in the harbour city.
examples.zh: 报界称这位航运「巨头」是港城最富有的人。

words.enDefinition: a formal notice ending a treaty or contract; public condemnation

examples.en: The government gave one year's notice of denunciation of the old trade treaty.
examples.zh: 政府提前一年发出通告，「废止」旧贸易条约。

examples.en: Her denunciation of the dumping scandal made headlines across the industry.
examples.zh: 她对倾销丑闻的「谴责」在整个行业上了头条。

words.enDefinition: exploit for maximal profit, usually by sacrificing quality

examples.en: Critics say the festival was commercialized once sponsors took over.
examples.zh: 批评者说，赞助商接手后这个节日就被「商业化」了。

examples.en: The lab hopes to commercialize its battery design within three years.
examples.zh: 实验室希望在三年内把电池设计「商业化」。

words.enDefinition: person or institution against whom an action is brought in a court of law; the person being sued or accused

examples.en: The defendant argued that the faulty wiring, not negligence, caused the fire.
examples.zh: 「被告」辩称，引发火灾的是线路故障，而非疏忽。

examples.en: In small-claims court, the defendant often represents himself without a lawyer.
examples.zh: 在小额索赔法庭上，「被告」常常不请律师自行辩护。

words.enDefinition: relating to or created by statutes

examples.en: Companies must hold a statutory audit once their turnover passes the limit.
examples.zh: 营业额超过限额后，公司必须进行「法定」审计。

examples.en: Employers must give statutory paid leave, even to part-time weekend staff.
examples.zh: 雇主必须提供「法定」带薪休假，兼职的周末员工也不例外。

words.enDefinition: separated in space or coming from or going to a distance

examples.en: The warehouse sits in a distant valley, so pickups start before four.
examples.zh: 仓库坐落在「遥远的」山谷里，所以四点前就得出发收货。

examples.en: Radio reached distant farms long before the telephone lines did.
examples.zh: 电话线路开通之前，「遥远的」农场早已靠无线电联络。

words.enDefinition: the act of admitting someone to enter

examples.en: Admission to the trade fair is free for members holding a valid badge.
examples.zh: 持有效证件的会员可免费「入场」参观商展会。

examples.en: Her admission to the wholesalers' association took nearly three months.
examples.zh: 她获得批发商协会的「接纳」花了近三个月。

words.enDefinition: the act of agreeing to or taking something offered; favourable approval

examples.en: The buyer signalled acceptance of our terms by paying the deposit early.
examples.zh: 买方提前支付定金，表明「接受」我们的条款。

examples.en: The product won wide acceptance among restaurants after one chef praised it.
examples.zh: 一位主厨称赞后，这款产品便在餐馆业赢得了广泛「认可」。

words.enDefinition: a rule or piece of advice that tells you how something should be done

examples.en: New hygiene guidelines require every baker to log oven temperatures twice daily.
examples.zh: 新的卫生「准则」要求每位烘焙师每天两次记录烤炉温度。

examples.en: The bank issued guidelines on lending to businesses affected by the floods.
examples.zh: 银行就向受洪灾影响的企业放贷发布了「指导方针」。

words.enDefinition: the carrying of goods, or the charge made for carrying them

examples.en: The invoice lists carriage at forty pounds for the two pallets.
examples.zh: 发票上列明两托盘货物的「运费」为四十英镑。

examples.en: Carriage of frozen goods needs vehicles fitted with working chillers.
examples.zh: 冷冻货物的「运输」需要装有正常制冷设备的车辆。

words.enDefinition: person who requests or seeks something such as assistance or employment or admission

examples.en: Each applicant must bring two references to the warehouse interview.
examples.zh: 每位「申请人」参加仓库面试时必须带两封推荐信。

examples.en: The grant scheme attracted an applicant from every county in the region.
examples.zh: 该补助计划吸引了全区每个县都有一名「申请者」。

words.enDefinition: (law) a gift of personal property by will

examples.en: The museum was built with a legacy from a local shipping family.
examples.zh: 这座博物馆是用当地一个航运家族的「遗赠」建造的。

examples.en: His legacy includes fair contracts that still protect pickers today.
examples.zh: 他留下的「遗产」包括至今仍保护采摘者的公平合同。

words.enDefinition: fundamental or basic; lying beneath or behind something else

examples.en: The report traced the delivery delays to an underlying problem with scheduling.
examples.zh: 报告把交货延误归结为排班方面一个「潜在的」问题。

examples.en: Beneath the noisy quarterly numbers lies an underlying demand for the alloy.
examples.zh: 在嘈杂的季度数字背后，是对这种合金「潜在的」需求。

words.enDefinition: (economics) a market in which there are many buyers but only one seller

examples.en: The utility lost its monopoly when the market opened to private generators.
examples.zh: 市场向私营发电商开放后，这家公用事业公司失去了「垄断」地位。

examples.en: Regulators fined the group for abusing its monopoly on rail freight.
examples.zh: 监管机构因该集团滥用铁路货运「垄断」权而对其罚款。

words.enDefinition: of or relating to statistics

examples.en: The statistical office publishes wage data for every region each spring.
examples.zh: 「统计」部门每年春季发布各地区的工资数据。

examples.en: Her statistical summary showed overtime costs doubling in winter months.
examples.zh: 她的「统计」摘要显示，冬季加班费翻了一番。

words.enDefinition: ensure observance of laws and rules;

examples.en: Council officers enforce the new parking rules from the first of March.
examples.zh: 市政人员从三月一日起「强制执行」新的停车规定。

examples.en: It is hard to enforce a no-smoking policy in an open-air market.
examples.zh: 在露天市场很难「执行」禁烟规定。

words.enDefinition: the basic structure or features of a system or organization

examples.en: Better road infrastructure would cut an hour off the dairy's morning run.
examples.zh: 更好的道路「基础设施」能为奶场每天的清晨运输省下一小时。

examples.en: The port upgrade is part of a national infrastructure plan for coastal trade.
examples.zh: 港口升级是国家沿海贸易「基础设施」计划的一部分。

words.enDefinition: an administrative unit of government

examples.en: The trade bureau handles complaints about late deliveries from abroad.
examples.zh: 贸易「局」负责处理来自海外的延迟交货投诉。

examples.en: She telephoned the statistics bureau to confirm the export figures.
examples.zh: 她打电话给统计「局」核实出口数据。

words.enDefinition: make known; pass on, of information

examples.en: Posters convey the safety rules better than a long speech ever could.
examples.zh: 海报「传达」安全规定的效果远胜冗长的讲话。

examples.en: A short email can convey the price change to every branch at once.
examples.zh: 一封简短的电子邮件就能把价格变动「传达到」所有分店。

words.enDefinition: a publicly stated opinion or position on an issue

examples.en: The retailer's stance on plastic packaging won praise from shoppers.
examples.zh: 这家零售商在塑料包装问题上的「立场」赢得了顾客称赞。

examples.en: Last quarter management took a firm stance against unpaid overtime.
examples.zh: 上季度管理层对无偿加班表明了坚决的「立场」。

words.enDefinition: following one after another without interruption

examples.en: Three successive harvests failed, pushing flour prices to a record.
examples.zh: 「连续」三季歉收，把面粉价格推到了历史新高。

examples.en: Successive governments promised to widen the canal but never funded it.
examples.zh: 「历届」政府都承诺拓宽运河，却从未拨款。

words.enDefinition: do away with

examples.en: The council voted to abolish the market tolls that traders had paid for decades.
examples.zh: 市政会投票「废除」商贩缴纳了几十年的市场通行费。

examples.en: The new manager abolished the old paper timesheets last month.
examples.zh: 新经理上个月「废除」了纸质考勤表。

words.enDefinition: an extra payment beyond usual salary; an unexpected pleasant extra

examples.en: Staff received a small bonus when the warehouse passed its safety audit.
examples.zh: 仓库通过安全审计后，员工收到了一笔小额「奖金」。

examples.en: The extra shelf space turned out to be a bonus for the bakery brand.
examples.zh: 多出来的货架空间对面包品牌来说是个意外「收获」。

words.enDefinition: to sign the back of a cheque or document; to publicly support or approve something

examples.en: The chef endorsed the new blender in a short video for the brand.
examples.zh: 主厨在品牌短视频里「代言」了新款搅拌机。

examples.en: Please endorse the cheque before paying it into the firm's account.
examples.zh: 把支票存入公司账户之前，请先在支票背面「背书」。

words.enDefinition: get involved, so as to alter or hinder an action, or through force or threat of force

examples.en: The bank had to intervene when the pound fell too fast that morning.
examples.zh: 那天早上英镑跌得太快，央行不得不出面「干预」。

examples.en: The supervisor intervened before the argument between the two drivers turned ugly.
examples.zh: 在两名司机的争吵升级之前，主管出面「调停」了。

words.enDefinition: command against

examples.en: Local rules prohibit stalls from selling fresh fish after midday in summer.
examples.zh: 当地规定「禁止」摊位在夏季午后售卖鲜鱼。

examples.en: The lease prohibits subletting any part of the warehouse without consent.
examples.zh: 未经同意，租约「禁止」转租仓库的任何部分。

words.enDefinition: required by rule

examples.en: Wearing safety goggles is compulsory for everyone inside the cutting workshop.
examples.zh: 切割车间内人人必须佩戴护目镜，这是「强制性」规定。

examples.en: Pension contributions became compulsory for all new employees this spring.
examples.zh: 今年春天起，所有新员工都必须「强制」缴纳养老金。

words.enDefinition: make oneself subject to; bring upon oneself; become liable to

examples.en: The firm incurred heavy fines after breaching the cold-chain rules twice.
examples.zh: 两次违反冷链规定后，这家公司「招致」了巨额罚款。

examples.en: Buyers who cancel late must incur the full cancellation charge.
examples.zh: 过晚取消订单的买家须「承担」全部取消费。

words.enDefinition: a person formally proposed or named for a position, award, or role

examples.en: Each branch puts forward a nominee for the staff representative seat.
examples.zh: 每个分店都推举一名「候选人」竞选职工代表席位。

examples.en: As executor, she is the nominee for the family trust documents.
examples.zh: 作为遗嘱执行人，她是家族信托文件的「被指定人」。

words.enDefinition: message that helps you remember something

examples.en: The third payment reminder arrived before the invoice was even due.
examples.zh: 发票还没到期，第三封「催款函」就到了。

examples.en: A note on the till serves as a reminder to check dates on chilled goods.
examples.zh: 收银台上的便条起到「提醒」作用，让人查看冷藏商品的日期。

words.enDefinition: the care and keeping of something or someone; protective charge

examples.en: The vault keeps client artwork in secure custody during the auction.
examples.zh: 拍卖期间，金库对客户艺术品实施安全「保管」。

examples.en: Documents held in the bank's custody may only leave with written consent.
examples.zh: 由银行「保管」的文件，须凭书面同意才能带出。

words.enDefinition: having no precedent; novel

examples.en: The port handled an unprecedented volume of timber after the new terminal opened.
examples.zh: 新码头启用后，港口的木材吞吐量达到「空前」水平。

examples.en: Demand for the insulation board rose at an unprecedented rate last winter.
examples.zh: 去年冬天，保温板的需求以「空前的」速度增长。

words.enDefinition: the business of providing services to tourists

examples.en: Winter tourism keeps the mountain hotels open when the ski season ends.
examples.zh: 滑雪季结束后，冬季「旅游业」让山上旅馆继续营业。

examples.en: The chamber of commerce credits tourism with saving the old harbour shops.
examples.zh: 商会认为「旅游业」救活了老港区的商铺。

words.enDefinition: substantial amount

examples.en: The logistics budget swallowed a huge chunk of the expansion fund.
examples.zh: 物流预算吞掉了扩张资金的很大「一块」。

examples.en: She cut the fruitcake into chunks before wrapping them as gifts.
examples.zh: 她把水果蛋糕切成「大块」，分别包好当礼物。

words.enDefinition: call in an official matter, such as to attend court

examples.en: The court summoned the warehouse manager to testify about the lost pallets.
examples.zh: 法院「传唤」仓库经理就丢失的托盘出庭作证。

examples.en: The board summoned an emergency meeting when the recall hit the news.
examples.zh: 召回事件见报后，董事会紧急「召集」了一次会议。

words.enDefinition: promoting or enhancing well-being

examples.en: The new rota proved beneficial for both the drivers and the customers.
examples.zh: 事实证明，新的排班表对司机和顾客都有「好处」。

examples.en: A short walk at lunch is beneficial to anyone working at a desk.
examples.zh: 午餐时散步片刻，对伏案工作的人大「有益处」。

words.enDefinition: make steady progress; be at the high point in one's career or reach a high point in historical significance or importance

examples.en: The corner shop thrives because it opens earlier than the supermarket.
examples.zh: 这家街角小店生意「兴旺」，因为它比超市开门更早。

examples.en: Some plants thrive in poor soil where better breeds quickly fail.
examples.zh: 有些植物在贫瘠土壤里也能「茁壮生长」，良种反而很快枯死。

words.enDefinition: relating or belonging to or characteristic of a municipality

examples.en: The municipal council repaved the market square before the summer fair.
examples.zh: 夏季集市开市前，「市政」会重新铺砌了市场广场。

examples.en: Municipal workers collected the stall refuse twice a day during the festival.
examples.zh: 节庆期间，「市政」工人每天两次清运摊位的垃圾。

words.enDefinition: of or concerned with or related to the future

examples.en: The agent showed three prospective buyers around the empty shop unit.
examples.zh: 中介带三位「有意向的」买家看了空置的店铺。

examples.en: We send samples to prospective clients before quoting a firm price.
examples.zh: 正式报价之前，我们会先给「潜在的」客户寄送样品。

words.enDefinition: grant authorization or clearance for

examples.en: Only the branch manager can authorize refunds above fifty pounds.
examples.zh: 只有分店经理才能「批准」五十英镑以上的退款。

examples.en: The ministry authorized the harbour to accept grain shipments at night.
examples.zh: 主管部门「授权」港口在夜间接收粮食船货。

words.enDefinition: goods carried by a large vehicle

examples.en: The crew secured the cargo of coffee sacks before the storm reached the bay.
examples.zh: 风暴进湾之前，船员固定好船上那批咖啡麻袋「货物」。

examples.en: Half the cargo shifted in the heavy swell, delaying the loading plan.
examples.zh: 巨浪中一半「货物」移位，打乱了装载计划。

words.enDefinition: prolonged intense look

examples.en: The tax office keeps small traders' accounts under close scrutiny.
examples.zh: 税务部门对小商贩的账目进行严密「审查」。

examples.en: Every figure in the tender faced scrutiny before the contract was awarded.
examples.zh: 授标之前，标书里的每个数字都经受了仔细「审查」。

words.enDefinition: properly or sufficiently qualified or capable or efficient

examples.en: We need a competent electrician to rewire the bakery before inspection.
examples.zh: 检查之前，我们需要一位「胜任的」电工给面包店重新布线。

examples.en: She is a competent negotiator who never promises dates she cannot keep.
examples.zh: 她是位「有能力的」谈判者，从不许下做不到的交期。

words.enDefinition: habitual or characteristic mental attitude that determines how you will interpret and respond to situations

examples.en: The chamber's outlook for autumn trade is cautiously optimistic this year.
examples.zh: 商会今年对秋季贸易的「展望」是谨慎乐观。

examples.en: Rainy weekends ruined the outlook for the beach vendors' season.
examples.zh: 连绵的雨周末毁了沙滩小贩对这一季的「预期」。

words.enDefinition: an economic state of growth with rising profits and full employment

examples.en: The canal brought prosperity to every mill along its banks.
examples.zh: 运河给两岸每家磨坊带来了「繁荣」。

examples.en: Locals date the town's prosperity from the day the railway arrived.
examples.zh: 当地人把小镇的「繁荣」归功于铁路通车的那一天。

words.enDefinition: implied though not directly expressed; inherent in the nature of something

examples.en: There was an implicit warning in the supplier's polite refusal to extend credit.
examples.zh: 供应商礼貌地拒绝延长账期，其中「暗含」警告。

examples.en: An implicit agreement keeps every stallholder to the same opening hours.
examples.zh: 一项不成文的「默契」让所有摊主遵守相同的营业时间。

words.enDefinition: meant to be kept secret or private; not for public disclosure

examples.en: Mark the payroll file confidential before it goes to the accountant.
examples.zh: 工资单文件送交会计之前，请标注「机密」。

examples.en: The supplier shared confidential pricing, trusting us not to leak it.
examples.zh: 供应商把「保密的」价格表交给我们，相信不会外泄。

words.enDefinition: an officer of a corporation or others who have access to private information about the corporation's operations

examples.en: An insider at the factory warned traders about the price rise weeks early.
examples.zh: 工厂的一名「内部人士」提前数周向贸易商透露了涨价消息。

examples.en: Only an insider could have known the export quota was about to open.
examples.zh: 只有「知情人」才知道出口配额即将开放。

words.enDefinition: caretaker for an apartment house; represents the owner as janitor and rent collector

examples.en: The building superintendent fixed the cold storage before the meat arrived.
examples.zh: 公寓「管理员」在肉品运到前修好了冷藏库。

examples.en: The works superintendent checks every batch before it leaves the yard.
examples.zh: 工地的「主管」在每批货物出库前都会检查。

words.enDefinition: formal document written for a prosecuting attorney charging a person with some offense

examples.en: The grand jury returned an indictment against the smuggling ring last week.
examples.zh: 大陪审团上周对走私团伙提出了「起诉书」。

examples.en: Reading the indictment aloud took the clerk nearly twenty minutes.
examples.zh: 书记员大声宣读这份「起诉书」用了将近二十分钟。

words.enDefinition: formal association of people with similar interests

examples.en: The bakers' guild sets training standards for every apprentice in the city.
examples.zh: 面包师「同业公会」为全城的学徒制定培训标准。

examples.en: Members of the guild meet quarterly to agree on flour prices.
examples.zh: 「公会」成员每季度碰头商定面粉价格。

words.enDefinition: occurring at or dependent on a particular season

examples.en: The cannery hires seasonal workers for the six-week peach harvest.
examples.zh: 罐头厂在为期六周的桃子收获季雇佣「季节工」。

examples.en: Ice-cream sales are highly seasonal, so stock is cut every October.
examples.zh: 冰淇淋销售「季节性」很强，所以每年十月都削减备货。

words.enDefinition: any animals kept for use or profit

examples.en: The market bans livestock deliveries during the hottest hours of July.
examples.zh: 市场禁止在七月最热时段运送「牲畜」。

examples.en: Trucking livestock overnight keeps the animals much cooler and calmer.
examples.zh: 夜间运输「牲畜」能让动物更凉爽、更安静。

words.enDefinition: an association of companies for some definite purpose

examples.en: A consortium of three builders won the contract to widen the dry dock.
examples.zh: 由三家建筑商组成的「联合体」赢得了扩建干船坞的合同。

examples.en: The airline joined a banking consortium to fund its new fleet.
examples.zh: 这家航空公司加入了一个银行「财团」，为新机队筹资。

words.enDefinition: contemptibly narrow in outlook

examples.en: Petty expenses like staples and tape are bought from the till float.
examples.zh: 订书钉、胶带这类「小额」杂项开支直接从备用现金里购买。

examples.en: The petty traders along the quay set up before the ferry docks.
examples.zh: 码头边的「小商贩」们在轮渡靠岸前就摆好了摊。

words.enDefinition: having decayed or disintegrated; usually implies foulness

examples.en: The grocer threw out a crate of rotten oranges before opening.
examples.zh: 杂货店开门前扔掉了一箱「腐烂的」橙子。

examples.en: Wooden pallets left in the rain go rotten within two winters.
examples.zh: 露天淋雨的木托盘过两个冬天就会「朽掉」。

words.enDefinition: of or relating to the system for delivering mail

examples.en: Postal delays pushed the catalogue launch back by a full week.
examples.zh: 「邮政」延误使产品目录的发布整整推迟了一周。

examples.en: The firm keeps a postal address in York for official letters.
examples.zh: 公司保留了一个约克的「邮寄」地址用于收发公函。

words.enDefinition: support through subsidies

examples.en: The region subsidizes night buses so market porters can get home safely.
examples.zh: 该地区「补贴」夜间巴士，让市场搬运工能安全回家。

examples.en: Grain imports were subsidized after two bad harvests in a row.
examples.zh: 连续两季歉收后，粮食进口获得了「资助」。

words.enDefinition: person who holds extreme views

examples.en: Police kept extremist groups away from the meat market on market day.
examples.zh: 集市日当天，警方阻止「极端分子」团体靠近肉类市场。

examples.en: The paper accused the protesters of listening to a few extremists.
examples.zh: 报纸指责抗议者听信了少数「极端分子」。

words.enDefinition: approve and express assent, responsibility, or obligation

examples.en: The senate voted to ratify the fishing accord with its neighbour.
examples.zh: 参议院投票「批准」与邻国的捕鱼协定。

examples.en: Members must ratify the merger before it can take effect.
examples.zh: 并购必须先由会员投票「批准」才能生效。

words.enDefinition: not conditional

examples.en: The firm offered an unconditional apology and refunded every affected order.
examples.zh: 公司作出「无条件」道歉，并退还所有受影响订单的货款。

examples.en: Their support for the strike fund was unconditional, without any strings.
examples.zh: 他们对罢工基金的支持是「无条件的」，不附带任何要求。

words.enDefinition: to express or include something as an essential or visible part

examples.en: The shop's hand-painted signs embody the owner's belief in slow craft.
examples.zh: 店铺的手绘招牌「体现」了店主对手工慢作的坚持。

examples.en: The new constitution embodies rights for small traders and market sellers.
examples.zh: 新章程「包含」了小商贩和集市卖家的各项权利。

words.enDefinition: not yet payable

examples.en: The court found undue pressure behind the farmer's signature on the lease.
examples.zh: 法庭认定农户在租约上签字时受到了「不当」压力。

examples.en: Charging interest before the invoice is due would be undue.
examples.zh: 发票未到期就计收利息，属于「未到期」收费。

words.enDefinition: person authorized to act for another

examples.en: She voted by proxy while recovering from surgery at home.
examples.zh: 她在家养伤期间由「代理人」代为投票。

examples.en: Shareholders who cannot attend may appoint a proxy before the meeting.
examples.zh: 无法出席的股东可在会前指定「代理」。

words.enDefinition: merchant who owns or manages a shop

examples.en: The tradesman who runs the ironmongery shop sponsored the rowing club.
examples.zh: 经营五金铺的这位「商人」赞助了划船俱乐部。

examples.en: Tradesmen in the arcade agreed to open late on Fridays.
examples.zh: 拱廊里的「店主们」商定每周五延长营业。

words.enDefinition: a place where things are stored; a person rich in information

examples.en: The archive is a repository of shipping records going back two centuries.
examples.zh: 这座档案馆是存放两个世纪以来航运记录的「宝库」。

examples.en: Grandma is a repository of recipes that the shop still bakes today.
examples.zh: 祖母简直是一座配方「宝库」，店里至今仍按她的配方烘焙。

words.enDefinition: a large public exhibition; a detailed explanation of a topic

examples.en: The dairy expo is the largest exposition of farm machinery in the county.
examples.zh: 乳品展是该县规模最大的农业机械「展览会」。

examples.en: Her short exposition of the export rules cleared up our confusion.
examples.zh: 她对出口规则的简明「阐述」解开了我们的疑惑。

words.enDefinition: performance of a musical composition or a dramatic role etc.

examples.en: The cellist's rendition of the old folk tune brought the hall to silence.
examples.zh: 大提琴手对那首老民谣的「演绎」让全场安静下来。

examples.en: His rendition of the national anthem opened the trade dinner.
examples.zh: 贸易晚宴以他对国歌的「演奏」开场。

words.enDefinition: the act of getting possession of something

examples.en: The procurement team compared four quotes before choosing the steel supplier.
examples.zh: 「采购」团队比较了四份报价后才选定钢材供应商。

examples.en: Public procurement rules require an advert in the local paper.
examples.zh: 公共「采购」规则要求在当地报纸上刊登公告。

words.enDefinition: one having charge of buildings or grounds or animals

examples.en: The custodian of the market hall locks the gates at nine each night.
examples.zh: 市场大厅的「管理员」每晚九点锁上大门。

examples.en: As custodian of the ledgers, she alone may open the archive room.
examples.zh: 作为账册的「保管人」，只有她能打开档案室。

words.enDefinition: of or relating to the economic system of mercantilism

examples.en: The mercantile exchange set coffee prices for the whole coast.
examples.zh: 这家「商业」交易所给整个海岸定出了咖啡价格。

examples.en: Liverpool grew rich on mercantile trade with the sugar islands.
examples.zh: 利物浦靠与蔗糖群岛的「商业」贸易致富。

words.enDefinition: of or relating to the function or responsibility or activity of management

examples.en: Managerial experience matters more than diplomas when hiring a floor supervisor.
examples.zh: 招聘车间主管时，「管理」经验比文凭更重要。

examples.en: The restructure created two new managerial posts at the depot.
examples.zh: 重组在货场新增了两个「管理」岗位。

words.enDefinition: someone who promotes or exchanges goods or services for money

examples.en: The marketer tested three slogans on shoppers at the outlet mall.
examples.zh: 这位「营销人员」在奥特莱斯商场对顾客测试了三条广告语。

examples.en: Good marketers ask customers questions instead of guessing the answers.
examples.zh: 优秀的「营销人员」会向顾客提问，而不是凭空猜测。

words.enDefinition: a warning to consider something before acting; a qualifying statement in a contract

examples.en: One caveat before you sign: the warranty excludes transport damage.
examples.zh: 签字前有个「注意事项」：质保不包括运输损坏。

examples.en: The contract carries a caveat about late delivery of the fittings.
examples.zh: 合同中有一条关于配件延迟交付的「警告」条款。

words.enDefinition: bear the expenses of

examples.en: The branch will defray the delivery charges for orders above two hundred pounds.
examples.zh: 订单超过两百英镑，分店将为客户「负担」运费。

examples.en: Sponsorships defray the cost of the youth football kit each season.
examples.zh: 赞助商每季「负担」少年足球队服的开支。

words.enDefinition: transactions (sales and purchases) having the objective of supplying commodities (goods and services)

examples.en: Locals complain that heavy commercialism has drained the market of its character.
examples.zh: 当地人抱怨浓重的「商业主义」气息让市场失去了本色。

examples.en: The magazine warns readers against pure commercialism in choosing a bank.
examples.zh: 杂志提醒读者，选银行时别被纯粹的「商业至上」论调牵着走。

words.enDefinition: an item given in part payment toward a new purchase

examples.en: The dealer offered three hundred pounds for our van as a trade-in.
examples.zh: 经销商对我们的货车给出三百英镑的「以旧换新」折价。

examples.en: Bring the old drill in; it still counts as a trade-in this month.
examples.zh: 把旧电钻带来，本月它仍可作「以旧换新」抵价。

words.enDefinition: person who brings an action in a court of law

examples.en: The plaintiff produced receipts proving the roof leaked within the warranty.
examples.zh: 「原告」出示了收据，证明屋顶在保修期内就漏雨。

examples.en: After three hearings, the plaintiff agreed to settle out of court.
examples.zh: 三次开庭后，「原告」同意庭外和解。

words.enDefinition: in law; the territory within which power can be exercised

examples.en: The dispute falls outside the tribunal's jurisdiction, so it moves to arbitration.
examples.zh: 这起争议不在仲裁庭的「管辖权」之内，将转交仲裁。

examples.en: Which court has jurisdiction over supply contracts signed at sea?
examples.zh: 在海上签署的供货合同归哪个法庭「管辖」？

words.enDefinition: form containing a set of questions; submitted to people to gain statistical information

examples.en: The survey team handed a questionnaire to every customer leaving the showroom.
examples.zh: 调研团队给每位走出展厅的顾客发了一份「调查问卷」。

examples.en: It took the shopkeeper ten minutes to complete the council's questionnaire.
examples.zh: 店主花十分钟就填完了市政会的「问卷」。

words.enDefinition: table (in a restaurant or bar) surrounded by two high-backed benches

examples.en: Our booth at the food fair sits right beside the tasting counter.
examples.zh: 美食节的「展位」就在试吃柜台旁边。

examples.en: Book your booth early; corner spots sell out by March.
examples.zh: 「展位」要早点订，转角位到三月就订光了。

words.enDefinition: change by sale or merger in the controlling interest of a corporation

examples.en: The takeover by a Dutch firm saved the shipyard but cut jobs.
examples.zh: 被一家荷兰公司「收购」救活了船厂，却也裁掉了岗位。

examples.en: Staff learned of the takeover from the morning papers, not from the board.
examples.zh: 员工是从晨报而非董事会得知「收购」消息的。

words.enDefinition: the customary manner in which a language (or a form of a language) is spoken or written

examples.en: Electricity usage doubles in December, so the deposit rises accordingly.
examples.zh: 十二月用电「量」翻倍，保证金也相应上调。

examples.en: The manual shows the correct usage of the dough press with photos.
examples.zh: 手册用照片演示压面机的正确「用法」。

words.enDefinition: the period during which a person holds an office, post, or right of occupancy

examples.en: During her tenure as manager, overtime claims fell by half.
examples.zh: 在她担任经理的「任期」内，加班申领减少了一半。

examples.en: The professor's tenure ended after twenty years at the fisheries institute.
examples.zh: 这位教授在渔业研究所二十年的「任期」结束了。

words.enDefinition: the classification of someone or something with respect to its worth

examples.en: The annual appraisal decides who gets the winter bonus this year.
examples.zh: 年度「考评」决定谁拿今年的冬季奖金。

examples.en: An independent appraisal valued the orchard at double last year's price.
examples.zh: 独立「评估」给果园的估值是去年价格的两倍。

words.enDefinition: required by law, rule, or authority; compulsory

examples.en: Steel-capped boots are mandatory for every worker inside the sawmill.
examples.zh: 锯木厂内人人必须穿钢头靴，这是「强制性」要求。

examples.en: Attendance at the fire drill is mandatory for all shift workers.
examples.zh: 所有轮班工人都「必须」参加消防演习。

words.enDefinition: the property of a more than adequate quantity or supply

examples.en: This year's abundance of plums lets the stall cut prices early.
examples.zh: 今年李子供应「充裕」，摊主早早降了价。

examples.en: An abundance of cheap imports squeezed the local weavers badly.
examples.zh: 廉价进口货「大量」涌入，让当地织工日子很难过。

words.enDefinition: written proposal or reminder

examples.en: The clerk circulated a memorandum about the new filing deadlines.
examples.zh: 文员传阅了一份关于新归档期限的「备忘录」。

examples.en: Sign the memorandum of understanding before the joint venture starts.
examples.zh: 合资项目启动前，先签署「谅解备忘录」。

words.enDefinition: an English coin worth one twentieth of a pound

examples.en: Grandfather paid one shilling for the haircut that started his barbershop career.
examples.zh: 祖父当年花一「先令」理发，从此开始了他的理发师生涯。

examples.en: The old ledgers record wages of twenty shillings a week.
examples.zh: 旧账本上记着每周二十「先令」的工钱。

words.enDefinition: formal command or admonition

examples.en: The judge issued an injunction halting demolition of the market hall.
examples.zh: 法官下达「禁令」，叫停市场大厅的拆除。

examples.en: The supplier ignored the injunction and shipped the copies anyway.
examples.zh: 供应商无视「强制令」，照样把仿品发了货。

words.enDefinition: plant where beer is brewed by fermentation

examples.en: The old brewery now rents its vaults to a cheese maker.
examples.zh: 老「啤酒厂」如今把地窖租给了一位奶酪师。

examples.en: Buses leave from the brewery gates for the hop fields.
examples.zh: 通勤班车从「啤酒厂」大门出发，前往啤酒花田。

words.enDefinition: low area where the land is saturated with water

examples.en: The farm's wetland attracts birds that help control the pests naturally.
examples.zh: 农场的「湿地」引来鸟类，天然帮忙控制虫害。

examples.en: Draining the wetland for a car park broke the planning rules.
examples.zh: 把「湿地」排干建停车场违反了规划法规。

words.enDefinition: added to complete or make up a deficiency

examples.en: Two supplementary shifts were added to cover the harvest fortnight.
examples.zh: 为赶收成，临时「增补」了两个班次。

examples.en: The bank asked for supplementary documents before approving the loan.
examples.zh: 银行要求先补交「附加」材料再审批贷款。

words.enDefinition: conformity with rules or standards

examples.en: The panel is known for its fairness when settling shop disputes.
examples.zh: 这个仲裁小组处理店铺纠纷时以「公正」著称。

examples.en: Workers accepted the rota once its fairness had been demonstrated.
examples.zh: 排班表证明其「公平」后，工人们接受了安排。

words.enDefinition: the custodian of a collection (as a museum or library)

examples.en: The curator arranged the trade tools by decade in the new wing.
examples.zh: 「馆长」把贸易工具按年代陈列在新展厅。

examples.en: Our curator borrowed a complete steam press for the printing display.
examples.zh: 「策展人」为印刷展借来了一台完整的蒸汽压机。

words.enDefinition: something that is regarded as a chance event

examples.en: The butcher runs a monthly lottery with a ham as first prize.
examples.zh: 肉铺每月举办一次「抽奖」，头奖是一整只火腿。

examples.en: Winning the export contract felt like winning the lottery, she said.
examples.zh: 她说，赢得出口合同就像中了「彩票」一样。

words.enDefinition: specific piece of work required to be done as a duty or for a specific fee

examples.en: Counting the till is the closing chore nobody in the shop enjoys.
examples.zh: 清点收银机是店里没人愿意干的收尾「杂务」。

examples.en: Feeding the hens is a morning chore before the market run.
examples.zh: 赶集之前，喂鸡是每天早晨的「琐事」。

words.enDefinition: an unintentional omission resulting from failure to notice something

examples.en: By a simple oversight, the invoice went out without the VAT number.
examples.zh: 纯属「疏忽」，发票寄出时忘了写增值税号。

examples.en: Checking the manifest twice prevented another oversight like last month's.
examples.zh: 舱单核对两遍，避免了再出现上个月那样的「疏漏」。

words.enDefinition: the support, especially regular custom, given by customers to a business

examples.en: The bakery owes its survival to the steady patronage of office workers.
examples.zh: 面包店能撑下来，全靠上班族稳定的「光顾」。

examples.en: Loyal patronage lets the bookseller order risky titles with confidence.
examples.zh: 有了老顾客的「惠顾」，书店才有底气进冷门书。

words.enDefinition: the practice of giving expert advice within a particular field

examples.en: Her consultancy advises small farms on cold storage and packing.
examples.zh: 她的「咨询公司」为小农场提供冷藏和包装方面的建议。

examples.en: He left the bank to start a two-person logistics consultancy.
examples.zh: 他离开银行，开办了一家两人的物流「咨询公司」。

words.enDefinition: in accordance with convention or custom

examples.en: A deposit of one fifth is customary when booking the marquee.
examples.zh: 预订大帐篷时付五分之一定金是「惯例」。

examples.en: It is customary here to tip the market porters at Christmas.
examples.zh: 当地「惯例」是圣诞节给市场搬运工小费。

words.enDefinition: person who carries a message

examples.en: A bicycle messenger carried the signed contract across the city at noon.
examples.zh: 中午，一名骑自行车的「信使」把签好的合同送过全城。

examples.en: Send the keys by messenger; do not leave them with the porter.
examples.zh: 钥匙请交给「送件人」带走，不要留给门房。

words.enDefinition: of words or propositions so related that each is the negation of the other

examples.en: The bakery and the cheese shop are complementary, not rivals.
examples.zh: 面包房和奶酪店是「互补」生意，不是对手。

examples.en: Her design skills and his engineering form a complementary partnership.
examples.zh: 她的设计功底与他的工程技术形成了「互补」搭档。

words.enDefinition: having no limits in range or scope

examples.en: The contract promises unlimited refills of the house filter coffee.
examples.zh: 合同承诺本店过滤咖啡「无限量」续杯。

examples.en: Unlimited overtime is not a plan; it is a warning sign.
examples.zh: 「无节制」的加班不是计划，而是警报。

words.enDefinition: an act of being a tenant or occupant

examples.en: Her tenancy of the flower stall runs to the end of September.
examples.zh: 她租下花摊的「租期」到九月底。

examples.en: The new tenancy agreement adds a clause about winter heating.
examples.zh: 新的「租赁」合同增加了冬季供暖条款。

words.enDefinition: protection against future loss

examples.en: The insurer granted full indemnity for the flooded storeroom last week.
examples.zh: 保险公司上周对被水淹的储藏室给予全额「赔偿」。

examples.en: Ask for an indemnity clause before moving the wine collection.
examples.zh: 搬运这批藏酒之前，先要求加入「免责赔偿」条款。

words.enDefinition: in fortunate circumstances financially; moderately rich

examples.en: The prosperous market garden supplies greens to three coastal towns.
examples.zh: 这家生意「兴隆的」市场菜园向三个海滨城镇供应蔬菜。

examples.en: Ferry links made the island prosperous within a single decade.
examples.zh: 轮渡通航后十年，小岛便「繁荣」起来。

words.enDefinition: not financially safe or secure

examples.en: Speculative buying pushed tin futures far above the factory price.
examples.zh: 「投机性」买入把锡期货价格推得远高于工厂售价。

examples.en: His speculative bid for the dockland site shocked the auction room.
examples.zh: 他对码头地块的「投机性」出价震惊了整个拍卖厅。

words.enDefinition: an allegation that something imposes an illegal obligation or denies some legal right or causes injustice

examples.en: The union filed a grievance over the new weekend rota.
examples.zh: 工会就新的周末排班提出了「申诉」。

examples.en: Every grievance gets a written reply within ten working days.
examples.zh: 每起员工「不满」投诉都会在十个工作日内书面答复。

words.enDefinition: restaurant where you serve yourself and pay a cashier

examples.en: The factory cafeteria serves soup and rolls until half past two.
examples.zh: 工厂「自助食堂」的汤一直供应到两点半。

examples.en: Renovating the staff cafeteria cut queue times at lunch by half.
examples.zh: 翻新员工「餐厅」后，午餐排队时间缩短了一半。

words.enDefinition: the state of being contingent on something

examples.en: A contingency fund covers ferry cancellations during the storm season.
examples.zh: 一笔「应急」基金用来应对风暴季的轮渡停航。

examples.en: The builder priced in a contingency for wet weekends on site.
examples.zh: 施工方在报价中留出了应对工地雨天的「意外」余量。

words.enDefinition: the guidance of ships or airplanes from place to place

examples.en: Heavy fog made navigation through the strait impossible until noon.
examples.zh: 中午之前大雾弥漫，海峡「航行」根本无法进行。

examples.en: Modern navigation kits let small fishing boats run at night safely.
examples.zh: 现代「导航」设备让小渔船能安全夜航。

words.enDefinition: relating to or having ability to think in or work with numbers

examples.en: The clerk's numerical error doubled the discount on the invoice.
examples.zh: 文员的「数字」错误把发票上的折扣翻了一倍。

examples.en: Applicants take a short numerical test before the interview round.
examples.zh: 面试环节之前，申请者要先做一项简短的「数字」测验。

words.enDefinition: characterized by speed; moving with or capable of moving with high speed

examples.en: Thanks to a speedy response, the spill never reached the harbour.
examples.zh: 由于「迅速」处置，泄漏物没有流入港口。

examples.en: We wish you a speedy recovery and a seat back on the team.
examples.zh: 祝你早日「康复」，早日回到团队。

words.enDefinition: the first event in a series

examples.en: A good opener gets the pitch noticed before anyone checks their phone.
examples.zh: 一个精彩的「开场白」能在别人掏手机之前就抓住注意力。

examples.en: The festival's opening night is the traditional opener for the tourist season.
examples.zh: 艺术节开幕之夜历来是旅游季的「开场戏」。

words.enDefinition: statute enacted by a city government

examples.en: A city ordinance bans market stalls from blocking the fire exits.
examples.zh: 市「条例」禁止市场摊位堵塞消防出口。

examples.en: Under the new ordinance, shops must display their opening hours outside.
examples.zh: 根据新「法令」，商店必须在门外张贴营业时间。

words.enDefinition: bordering on or living or characteristic of those near the sea

examples.en: The maritime museum charts a century of coasting trade routes.
examples.zh: 这座「海事」博物馆绘制了一个世纪的沿海贸易航线。

examples.en: Every maritime insurance claim needs a copy of the cargo manifest.
examples.zh: 每宗「海事」保险索赔都需要一份舱单副本。

words.enDefinition: continuing forever or indefinitely

examples.en: The lease grants a perpetual right of way across the mill yard.
examples.zh: 租约授予穿过磨坊场院的「永久」通行权。

examples.en: Their perpetual bargaining wore out every supplier in the district.
examples.zh: 他们「没完没了的」讨价还价磨光了本地区所有供应商的耐心。

words.enDefinition: confer a trust upon

examples.en: We entrust only the night safe keys to the senior cashier.
examples.zh: 我们只把夜间保险箱钥匙「托付」给资深出纳。

examples.en: Parents entrust the school with their children's lunch money each week.
examples.zh: 家长们每周把孩子的午餐钱「交给」学校保管。

words.enDefinition: avoiding waste

examples.en: The smaller van is economical to run, saving us petrol every week.
examples.zh: 小型货车开起来「省油」，每周都帮我们省下汽油钱。

examples.en: Buying flour in sacks is more economical than small packets.
examples.zh: 整袋买面粉比小包装更「划算」。

words.enDefinition: the face value of a currency note, coin, or security

examples.en: The cashier keeps small denominations ready for the morning bus fares.
examples.zh: 收银员备好小「面额」钞票，方便早上找零公共汽车票钱。

examples.en: Church collections record every denomination, down to the copper coins.
examples.zh: 教会募捐记录每一种「面值」，连铜板也不放过。

words.enDefinition: to fulfil a promise or an obligation

examples.en: Customers can redeem these vouchers at any branch before Christmas.
examples.zh: 顾客可在圣诞节前于任何分店「兑换」这些代金券。

examples.en: He redeemed his promise to reopen the workshop within a month.
examples.zh: 他「兑现」了一个月内重开作坊的承诺。

words.enDefinition: made of or containing metal

examples.en: A metallic taste in the tap water prompted tests at the pumping station.
examples.zh: 自来水里有股「金属」味，泵站随即安排了检测。

examples.en: The artist paints with metallic inks that catch the shop window light.
examples.zh: 艺术家用带「金属光泽」的墨水作画，正好映衬橱窗的光。

words.enDefinition: undergoing no change when acted upon

examples.en: The coastal depot stayed unaffected by the rail strikes last week.
examples.zh: 上周铁路罢工期间，沿海货场的运营「未受影响」。

examples.en: Her pricing stayed unaffected by the rumours circling the trade.
examples.zh: 四处流传的行情传闻让她的定价依然「不受影响」。

words.enDefinition: act of turning to for assistance

examples.en: Small shops have little recourse when a wholesaler collapses with their deposits.
examples.zh: 批发商卷走定金倒闭时，小店铺几乎没有「追索」途径。

examples.en: The contract leaves us no recourse but to wait out the delay.
examples.zh: 合同没给我们留任何「追索权」，只能干等延误结束。

words.enDefinition: the remaining parts of something that has been wrecked

examples.en: Divers photographed the wreckage of the coal barge near the breakwater.
examples.zh: 潜水员拍下了防波堤附近运煤驳船的「残骸」。

examples.en: The garage towed the wreckage off the coast road before rush hour.
examples.zh: 高峰期之前，修车厂把事故「残骸」拖离了滨海公路。

words.enDefinition: deliberately avoiding; keeping away from or preventing from happening

examples.en: Tax avoidance through offshore accounts drew sharp questions at the hearing.
examples.zh: 听证会上，通过离岸账户「避税」的做法遭到尖锐质询。

examples.en: His careful avoidance of the wet paint saved the new sign.
examples.zh: 他小心「避开」未干的油漆，保住了新招牌。

words.enDefinition: grow by addition

examples.en: Interest will accrue on the loan from the day the ship sails.
examples.zh: 贷款利息自船只开航之日起开始「累积」。

examples.en: Loyalty points accrue faster on wholesale orders than retail ones.
examples.zh: 批发订单的会员积分「累积」速度比零售快。

words.enDefinition: the property of being an amount by which something is less than expected or required

examples.en: A shortfall in donor funds delayed the new ambulance by months.
examples.zh: 捐款「缺口」使新救护车的采购推迟了几个月。

examples.en: The harvest left a shortfall of two hundred tonnes for the contract.
examples.zh: 这次收成使合同出现了两百吨的「亏空」。

words.enDefinition: relating to the mood of verbs that is used simple in declarative statements

examples.en: Send an indicative price first; the firm quote follows the survey.
examples.zh: 先发一个「参考」价，勘察之后再报实价。

examples.en: Their cautious tone was indicative of a long negotiation ahead.
examples.zh: 他们谨慎的语气「表明」前面还有一场漫长的谈判。

words.enDefinition: not safe; involving risk of harm, loss, or failure

examples.en: The inspector declared the scaffolding unsafe after two days of storms.
examples.zh: 风暴过后两天，检查员宣布脚手架「不安全」。

examples.en: Stacking crates above head height is unsafe in a busy aisle.
examples.zh: 在繁忙通道把货箱堆过头顶很「危险」。

words.enDefinition: payment or reward (especially from a government) for acts such as catching criminals or killing predatory animals or enlisting in the military

examples.en: The government pays a bounty for every fox-proof fence installed.
examples.zh: 政府为每个防狐围栏发放「奖励金」。

examples.en: A bounty of fifty pounds drew dozens of volunteers to the river clean-up.
examples.zh: 五十英镑的「赏金」吸引了几十名志愿者参加河道清理。

words.enDefinition: water falling in drops from vapor condensed in the atmosphere

examples.en: This month's rainfall already tops the whole of last summer.
examples.zh: 本月的「降雨量」已经超过去年整个夏天。

examples.en: Low rainfall pushed hay prices up before the fair even opened.
examples.zh: 集市还没开，「降雨量」偏少就抬高了干草价格。

words.enDefinition: something owned; any tangible or intangible possession that is owned by someone;

examples.en: Staff must keep their belongings in the lockers, not under the counter.
examples.zh: 员工必须把「随身物品」放进储物柜，不能塞在柜台下面。

examples.en: She gathered her belongings and left the workshop for the last time.
examples.zh: 她收拾好「个人物品」，最后一次离开了作坊。

words.enDefinition: skilled worker who practices some trade or handicraft

examples.en: Each artisan signs the bottom of the bowls thrown in this studio.
examples.zh: 这间工作室出的每只碗，底部都有「工匠」的签名。

examples.en: The shop is run by an artisan who still cuts glass by hand.
examples.zh: 店主是一位仍坚持手工切割玻璃的「手艺人」。

words.enDefinition: having many parts or sides

examples.en: A multilateral deal cut tariffs for every port on the route.
examples.zh: 一项「多边」协议为航线上的所有港口削减了关税。

examples.en: Multilateral talks on freight standards resume in Geneva next month.
examples.zh: 货运标准的「多边」会谈下月在日内瓦重启。

words.enDefinition: tending to float on a liquid or rise in air or gas

examples.en: Cork floats because it is naturally buoyant even when soaked.
examples.zh: 软木即使泡透也能浮着，因为它天生「有浮力」。

examples.en: Buoyant demand for bicycles kept the hire shop open all winter.
examples.zh: 自行车需求「火爆」，租车店整个冬天都没歇业。

words.enDefinition: distance measured in miles

examples.en: The van's mileage doubled once we added the Friday market run.
examples.zh: 加了周五集市路线后，货车的「里程」翻了一倍。

examples.en: She claims mileage from the depot to every farm she audits.
examples.zh: 她按从货场到每个受审农场的「英里数」报销车费。

words.enDefinition: the charge for mailing something

examples.en: The postage on our sample boxes rose again this January.
examples.zh: 今年一月，样品箱的「邮费」又涨了。

examples.en: We always add postage to the invoice for mail-order deliveries.
examples.zh: 邮购订单的「邮资」会计入发票。

words.enDefinition: small and inadequate amount

examples.en: Scarcity of clean water raised the price of bottled stock at the depot.
examples.zh: 净水的「稀缺」抬高了货站瓶装水的价格。

examples.en: A scarcity of seasonal pickers left half the orchard unpicked.
examples.zh: 采摘工「短缺」让半个果园的果子无人摘收。

words.enDefinition: a formal or official announcement or notice

examples.en: You will get a notification when the repaired till is ready.
examples.zh: 修好的收银机好了，你会收到「通知」。

examples.en: Ten days' written notification is required before closing the stall.
examples.zh: 歇业摊位须提前十天发出书面「通知」。

words.enDefinition: slow-moving; (of a market or business) not active or brisk

examples.en: Sales stayed sluggish through February, with hardly any weekend custom.
examples.zh: 二月份生意「萧条」，周末几乎没什么客人。

examples.en: The sluggish ferry service pushed shoppers toward the inland mall.
examples.zh: 「迟缓的」轮渡服务把购物者推向了内陆商场。

words.enDefinition: do without or cease to hold or adhere to

examples.en: The hotel waived the cancellation fee because of the ferry strike.
examples.zh: 因轮渡罢工，酒店「免除」了取消费。

examples.en: Suppliers rarely waive the minimum-order rule for brand new shops.
examples.zh: 供应商很少为新店铺「放弃」最低起订量的规定。

words.enDefinition: written declaration made under oath; a written statement sworn to be true before someone legally authorized to administer an oath

examples.en: The witness signed an affidavit swearing she saw the truck leave at six.
examples.zh: 证人签署了一份「宣誓书」，保证自己六点看见卡车离开。

examples.en: The bank requires a signed affidavit before releasing the estate funds.
examples.zh: 银行要求先提交签署的「宣誓书」才发放遗产资金。

words.enDefinition: something immaterial that interferes with or delays action or progress

examples.en: Poor harbour access is the main impediment to bigger cruise calls.
examples.zh: 港口通道不畅是大型邮轮靠泊的主要「障碍」。

examples.en: A speech impediment never held him back at client meetings.
examples.zh: 言语「障碍」从未影响他出席客户会议。

words.enDefinition: to enlarge beyond bounds or the truth

examples.en: The brochure overstates the van's range; flat hills drain the battery faster.
examples.zh: 宣传册「夸大」了货车的续航，平缓的坡地更耗电池。

examples.en: Do not overstate the savings; buyers will test every claim.
examples.zh: 别「夸大」节省的金额，买家会逐条验证。

words.enDefinition: making something valid by formally ratifying or confirming it

examples.en: Parliament's ratification of the harbour deal took eleven long months.
examples.zh: 议会「正式批准」港口协议花了十一个月。

examples.en: Union members still await ratification of the new shift agreement.
examples.zh: 工会会员正等待「批准」新的轮班协议。

words.enDefinition: past due; not paid at the scheduled time

examples.en: The third reminder says our account is two weeks overdue.
examples.zh: 第三份催款单说我们的账款已「逾期」两周。

examples.en: Return the pressure washer before Friday or it counts as overdue.
examples.zh: 高压清洗机周五前归还，否则按「过期」计。

words.enDefinition: to send goods to a person or place to be sold or forwarded

examples.en: The potter consigns her bowls to the gallery rather than selling direct.
examples.zh: 陶艺师把碗「寄售」给画廊，而不是直接销售。

examples.en: The farm consigns its cheese to the city market every Thursday.
examples.zh: 农场每周四把奶酪「托运」进城销售。

words.enDefinition: fraudulent; having a misleading appearance

examples.en: A bogus inspector tried to charge shops for fake safety checks.
examples.zh: 一名「假冒的」检查员想向店铺收取假安全检查费。

examples.en: The bogus fifty-pound notes fooled two tills before the bank flagged them.
examples.zh: 「伪造的」五十英镑假币骗过两台收银机后才被银行识别。

words.enDefinition: solidify, firm, or strengthen

examples.en: The auditor asked us to substantiate every travel claim with receipts.
examples.zh: 审计师要求我们用收据「证实」每一笔差旅报销。

examples.en: Rumours of a buyout were never substantiated by the board.
examples.zh: 董事会从未「证实」过收购传闻。

words.enDefinition: not limited or restricted

examples.en: She gave the design her unqualified approval and ordered a full print run.
examples.zh: 她对设计「毫无保留」地认可，并下令全量印制。

examples.en: Unqualified praise from the food magazine doubled our weekend bookings.
examples.zh: 杂志「毫无保留的」称赞让周末预订翻倍。

words.enDefinition: evaluate or estimate the nature, quality, ability, extent, or significance of

examples.en: An expert came to appraise the collection before the estate sale.
examples.zh: 遗产拍卖前，一位专家前来「估价」这批藏品。

examples.en: Managers appraise each trainee's progress at the end of the month.
examples.zh: 月底时，经理们会「评估」每位学员的进步。

words.enDefinition: to refuse to accept, acknowledge, or honour as valid, especially a claim, debt, or obligation

examples.en: The buyer repudiated the contract when the bolts failed the third test.
examples.zh: 螺栓第三次检测不合格后，买方「拒绝履行」合同。

examples.en: The heirs repudiate any claim that grandfather owed the bank money.
examples.zh: 继承人「否认」祖父欠银行钱的说法。

words.enDefinition: pay back for some expense incurred

examples.en: The firm will reimburse your train fare if you keep the ticket.
examples.zh: 只要保留车票，公司就会给你「报销」火车费。

examples.en: We reimbursed the customer in full after the cooler arrived damaged.
examples.zh: 冷藏箱到货损坏后，我们向顾客作了全额「赔付」。

words.enDefinition: an accounting account used to hold items pending classification

examples.en: The mystery payment sits in the suspense account until the clerk sorts it out.
examples.zh: 这笔来路不明的款项先挂在「暂记」账户，等文员查明。

examples.en: A suspense account caught the duplicate rent transfer for three weeks.
examples.zh: 一个「暂记」账户挂了三周重复划转的租金。

words.enDefinition: piece of unexpected good fortune, especially a sudden financial gain

examples.en: The land sale brought the village a windfall of half a million pounds.
examples.zh: 卖地给村子带来五十万英镑的「意外之财」。

examples.en: A windfall tax cut into the energy company's surprise profits.
examples.zh: 「暴利」税削减了能源公司意外所得的利润。

words.enDefinition: not growing or changing; without force or vitality

examples.en: Trade has been stagnant since the mill closed last autumn.
examples.zh: 自去年秋天磨坊关闭以来，生意一直「停滞」。

examples.en: Wages stayed stagnant while rents kept climbing in the port district.
examples.zh: 港区租金一路上涨，工资却原地「踏步」。

words.enDefinition: criminal falsification by making or altering an instrument with intent to defraud

examples.en: Police confirmed the signature on the bill of sale was a forgery.
examples.zh: 警方确认买卖单据上的签名是「伪造的」。

examples.en: The gallery quietly withdrew two paintings suspected of being forgeries.
