examples.zh: 画廊悄悄撤下了两幅疑为「赝品」的画作。

words.enDefinition: secret agreement

examples.en: The fuel distributors firmly denied collusion on the regional price lists.
examples.zh: 燃油经销商坚决否认在地区价目单上存在「串通」。

examples.en: Two bidders were banned after evidence of collusion at the tender.
examples.zh: 投标中出现「勾结」证据后，两家投标人被禁赛。

words.zhGloss: 招股说明书；发售说明书
words.enDefinition: formal written offer to sell securities (filed with the SEC) that sets forth a plan for a (proposed) business enterprise
acceptedZhAnswers: 招股说明书；发售说明书

examples.en: Read the prospectus carefully before you put savings into the bond.
examples.zh: 把积蓄投入债券前，请仔细阅读「招股说明书」。

examples.en: The bakery's prospectus promised three new shops within two years.
examples.zh: 面包店的「发售说明书」承诺两年内新开三家门店。

words.enDefinition: diplomat appointed by a government to protect its commercial interests and help its citizens in a foreign country

examples.en: The consul helped the crew recover their wages in a foreign port.
examples.zh: 「领事」帮船员在外国港口讨回了工资。

examples.en: Trade complaints go through the consul's office before reaching the ministry.
examples.zh: 贸易投诉先经「领事馆」办公室处理，再转交主管部门。

words.enDefinition: one that is absent or not in residence

examples.en: Friday's shift had three absentees, so the depot ran short-handed.
examples.zh: 周五的班次有三名「缺勤者」，货场人手不足。

examples.en: The landlord chased every absentee tenant about the winter rent.
examples.zh: 房东向每位「不在场的」租户追讨冬季租金。

words.enDefinition: compensation (given or received) for an insult or injury

examples.en: The court ordered the factory to pay reparation for the polluted stream.
examples.zh: 法院责令工厂为污染的溪流支付「赔偿」。

examples.en: Full reparation for the smashed crates was settled within a week.
examples.zh: 砸坏货箱的全部「赔偿」一周内就结清了。

words.enDefinition: stating an amount as less than it actually is, especially in accounts or tax

examples.en: The auditor called the missing fuel log an understatement of costs.
examples.zh: 审计员称缺失的燃料记录是对成本的「少报」。

examples.en: Reporting the vintage as one crate was a deliberate understatement.
examples.zh: 把那批年份酒报成一箱是刻意的「少报」。

words.enDefinition: stone that is used to mark a grave

examples.en: The stonemason carved the merchant's name deep into the tombstone.
examples.zh: 石匠把这位商人的名字深深刻进「墓碑」。

examples.en: Lichen covered the old tombstones along the churchyard's east wall.
examples.zh: 教堂院墙东边的旧「墓碑」上长满了地衣。

words.enDefinition: assets that are saleable though not material or physical

examples.en: Goodwill is an intangible asset, yet it sold the bakery for more.
examples.zh: 商誉是一种「无形」资产，却让面包店卖出了更高价。

examples.en: Reputation still counts as intangible value on most balance sheets.
examples.zh: 声誉在大多数资产负债表上仍属于「无形」价值。

words.enDefinition: consisting of a haphazard assortment of different kinds

examples.en: A sundry box in the storeroom holds string, labels, and spare keys.
examples.zh: 储藏室的「杂物」盒里装着细绳、标签和备用钥匙。

examples.en: Sundry debts under fifty pounds were written off in March.
examples.zh: 三月里，五十英镑以下的「杂项」欠款被核销了。

words.enDefinition: the quality of being fraudulent

examples.en: Selling margarine as butter is plain deceit, the inspector said.
examples.zh: 检验员说，把人造黄油当黄油卖纯粹是「欺骗」。

examples.en: Years of small deceits finally collapsed the whole trading partnership.
examples.zh: 多年的小小「欺诈」最终拖垮了这家贸易合伙行。

words.enDefinition: activity involved in maintaining something in good working order

examples.en: Monthly upkeep of the cold room costs more than the electricity.
examples.zh: 冷藏间每月的「养护」费用比电费还高。

examples.en: The tenant covers internal upkeep while the landlord repairs the roof.
examples.zh: 租户承担室内「维护」，屋顶修缮归房东。

words.enDefinition: not producing or capable of producing

examples.en: An unproductive afternoon of meetings cost the depot a delivery run.
examples.zh: 一下午开会毫无「产出」，害得货场少跑一趟送件。

examples.en: The northern field is unproductive, so we graze sheep there instead.
examples.zh: 北边那块地「长不出东西」，我们改在那里放羊。

words.enDefinition: any heavy material used to stabilize a ship or airship

examples.en: Gravel served as ballast until the timber cargo was loaded at noon.
examples.zh: 中午木材装船之前，先用砂石充当「压舱物」。

examples.en: Shifting ballast in the storm tilted the old barge dangerously.
examples.zh: 风暴中「压舱物」移位，旧驳船险情骤起。

words.enDefinition: remote and undeveloped area

examples.en: Farmers from the green hinterland bring butter to the coast market weekly.
examples.zh: 绿色「腹地」的农户每周把黄油带到海边市场。

examples.en: The port grew rich by taxing goods moving into its hinterland.
examples.zh: 港口靠对运入「腹地」的货物征税而致富。

words.enDefinition: cancel officially

examples.en: The board voted to rescind the parking levy after the protests.
examples.zh: 抗议之后，董事会投票「撤销」了停车税。

examples.en: The college rescinded the offer when the transcripts failed to arrive.
examples.zh: 成绩单迟迟未到，学院「取消」了录取通知。

words.enDefinition: formal or authoritative proclamation

examples.en: The mayor's edict ordered all stalls shut by eight each evening.
examples.zh: 市长的「法令」要求所有摊位每晚八点前收摊。

examples.en: An imperial edict opened the river trade to every licensed boat.
examples.zh: 一纸「敕令」向所有持照船只开放了内河贸易。

words.enDefinition: deprive of by deceit

examples.en: The pair defrauded pensioners out of savings with a fake roof repair.
examples.zh: 两人用假屋顶维修「骗取」了养老金领取者的积蓄。

examples.en: Companies that defraud buyers face bans under trading standards rules.
examples.zh: 「欺诈」买家的公司将依据交易标准法规被禁业。

words.enDefinition: contestant (human or animal) not considered to have a good chance to win

examples.en: As an outsider to the trade, he asked questions buyers never dared.
examples.zh: 作为业外「外人」，他问出了买家从不敢问的问题。

examples.en: Outsiders rarely get to see how the fish auctions really run.
examples.zh: 「行外人」很少能看到鱼类拍卖的真实运作。

words.enDefinition: the act of throwing cargo overboard to save a ship; discarding something burdensome

examples.en: The captain ordered the jettison of half the cargo to save the brig.
examples.zh: 为保住双桅船，船长下令「弃掉」一半货物。

examples.en: They jettisoned the plan for a second pier after the survey.
examples.zh: 勘察之后，他们「放弃」了修建第二个码头的计划。

words.enDefinition: without cause

examples.en: The lawyer's gratuitous advice saved the stallholder a court fee.
examples.zh: 律师「无偿的」指点为摊主省下了一笔诉讼费。

examples.en: Critics called the extra charges gratuitous, with no service behind them.
examples.zh: 批评者称这些「无缘无故」加收的费用背后并无任何服务。

words.enDefinition: person who has deposited money in a bank or similar institution

examples.en: Each depositor at the credit union is covered up to the limit.
examples.zh: 信用社的每位「存款人」都在限额内受到保障。

examples.en: The bank wrote to every depositor about the new branch hours.
examples.zh: 银行致函每位「储户」，告知新的营业时间。

words.enDefinition: have and control fully and exclusively

examples.en: One mill family monopolized flour milling across the whole valley.
examples.zh: 一家磨坊家族「垄断」了整个山谷的面粉研磨。

examples.en: Don't let one client monopolize your whole week of deliveries.
examples.zh: 别让一个客户「独占」你整周的配送时段。

words.enDefinition: so high or severe that it prevents something from being done or bought

examples.en: Cold storage fees are prohibitive in summer, so she sells fast.
examples.zh: 夏季冷藏费「贵得吓人」，所以她快进快出。

examples.en: Prohibitive parking charges pushed many shoppers to the out-of-town mall.
examples.zh: 「高得离谱」的停车费把许多购物者推向了城外商场。

words.enDefinition: incapable of being retracted or revoked

examples.en: Once you sign, the transfer becomes irrevocable under the new rules.
examples.zh: 按新规，签署之后转让即「不可撤销」。

examples.en: He called the acceptance letter irrevocable and booked the shipper.
examples.zh: 他说这份接受函「不可撤销」，随即预订了承运人。

words.enDefinition: lacking zest or vivacity

examples.en: The listless afternoon crowd left the vendors checking their phones.
examples.zh: 午后人群「无精打采」，摊主们只好刷起了手机。

examples.en: A listless welcome at the door cost the shop its regulars.
examples.zh: 门口「有气无力的」待客方式赶走了店里的老主顾。

words.enDefinition: acting or arriving or performed exactly at the time appointed

examples.en: The punctual milk float still arrives before the shops open.
examples.zh: 「准时的」送奶车仍在店铺开门前抵达。

examples.en: Being punctual at the fish auction means first choice of the catch.
examples.zh: 在鱼类拍卖场「守时」意味着能优先挑货。

words.enDefinition: the fraudulent appropriation of funds or property entrusted to your care but actually owned by someone else

examples.en: The treasurer was arrested for embezzlement of the raffle money.
examples.zh: 财务主管因「侵吞」抽奖款而被捕。

examples.en: Auditors uncovered embezzlement after two van payments went astray in spring.
examples.zh: 春天两笔购车款去向不明后，审计人员查出了「贪污」。

words.enDefinition: represented or appearing as such; pretended

examples.en: The inspection's ostensible purpose was safety; finding accounts came second.
examples.zh: 这次检查「名义上」为安全，查账才是其次。

examples.en: His ostensible reason for visiting was a broken freezer door.
examples.zh: 他来访「表面上」是为了那扇坏了的冰柜门。

words.enDefinition: strike in which the workers walk out

examples.en: A one-hour walkout delayed every delivery from the depot on Tuesday.
examples.zh: 周二一小时的「罢工」让货场的所有派送都延误了。

examples.en: The kitchen walkout ended once the owner restored the Sunday pay.
examples.zh: 老板恢复周日工资后，后厨「罢工」结束了。

words.enDefinition: make less central

examples.en: The chain plans to decentralize purchasing, giving each region its own buyers.
examples.zh: 连锁企业计划将采购「分权」，让各地区自设采购员。

examples.en: They decentralized the accounts office into three smaller regional hubs.
examples.zh: 他们把会计室「下放」为三个更小的地区中心。

words.enDefinition: someone chosen to judge and decide a disputed issue

examples.en: The arbitrator heard both carriers before fixing the shared berth fees.
examples.zh: 「仲裁人」听取两家承运方陈述后，确定了共用泊位费。

examples.en: An independent arbitrator settled the dispute over the rotten shipment.
examples.zh: 一位独立「仲裁员」了结了腐烂货物的纠纷。

words.enDefinition: an increase to counteract a perceived discrepancy

examples.en: The contract allows an annual escalation of storage fees with inflation.
examples.zh: 合同允许仓储费随通胀逐年「上调」。

examples.en: Quick talks last week prevented an escalation of the pricing dispute.
examples.zh: 上周的快速谈判阻止了价格争端的「升级」。

words.enDefinition: document effecting a property transfer

examples.en: The solicitor drafted the conveyance for the old mill and its yard.
examples.zh: 律师为老磨坊及其场院起草了「产权转让契据」。

examples.en: Sign the conveyance on Friday; the keys pass at noon.
examples.zh: 周五签署「转让契据」，钥匙中午交接。

words.enDefinition: being in demand by especially employers

examples.en: Apprenticeships turn raw helpers into marketable tradespeople within two years.
examples.zh: 学徒制能在两年内把新手培养成「抢手的」技工。

examples.en: The surplus wool is marketable if we clean and grade it first.
examples.zh: 多余羊毛只要先洗净分级就很「有销路」。

words.enDefinition: expend, as from a fund

examples.en: The treasurer disburses the float every Monday morning against receipts.
examples.zh: 财务每周一早晨凭收据「拨付」备用金。

examples.en: Grants were disbursed to the ferry fund after the audit.
examples.zh: 审计之后，补助金「拨付」给了轮渡基金。

words.enDefinition: someone who makes an offer

examples.en: The highest bidder took the pallets of tinned pears at noon.
examples.zh: 中午，出价最高的「竞买人」拍走了整托盘的罐装梨。

examples.en: One bidder asked to inspect the engines before the auction opened.
examples.zh: 拍卖开始前，一位「投标人」要求先查验那批发动机。

words.enDefinition: stock broker's business; charges a fee to act as intermediary between buyer and seller

examples.en: The brokerage earns its fee on every charter it fixes for us.
examples.zh: 这间「经纪行」按撮合的每份租船合同收取佣金。

examples.en: She left the city brokerage to run the family freight firm.
examples.zh: 她离开城里的「经纪公司」，回家经营家族货运生意。

words.enDefinition: relating to the near future

examples.en: The short-range forecast promises three dry days for the harvest.
examples.zh: 「短期」预报显示未来三天天气晴好，适合收割。

examples.en: Short-range planning covers the summer fair; the depot expansion is longer term.
examples.zh: 「近期」规划涵盖夏季集市；货场扩建则是更长远的事。

words.enDefinition: farmer who breed or raises livestock

examples.en: The stockman moves the herd to the high pasture every June.
examples.zh: 「牲畜饲养员」每年六月把牛群赶到高地牧场。

examples.en: A good stockman notices a lame ewe long before the vet does.
examples.zh: 好的「牧场工人」比兽医更早发现跛脚的母羊。

words.enDefinition: not conducive to commercial success

examples.en: The treasurer admits the mural fund is kindly but uncommercial.
examples.zh: 保留那幅褪色壁画是善意之举，却「无商业价值」。

examples.en: The new manager called the free teas for tramps uncommercial.
examples.zh: 新经理说，给流浪汉免费上茶这种做法「不赚钱」。

words.enDefinition: the act of intervening (as to mediate a dispute, etc.)

examples.en: Quick intervention by the harbourmaster saved the pontoon from drifting.
examples.zh: 港务长及时「介入」，救回了漂走的浮桥。

examples.en: Government intervention held the ferry fares flat through the summer.
examples.zh: 政府「干预」让轮渡票价整个夏天保持不变。

words.enDefinition: something (as a course of action) that is recommended as advisable

examples.en: On the vet's recommendation, we switched the herd to morning milking.
examples.zh: 根据兽医的「建议」，我们把牛群改为早晨挤奶。

examples.en: Her recommendation of the new tills carried weight with the board.
examples.zh: 她对新型收银机的「推荐」在董事会很有分量。

words.enDefinition: the act or process of finishing something

examples.en: Completion of the cold store slipped a week behind schedule.
examples.zh: 冷库的「完工」比计划推迟了一周。

examples.en: Payment is due on completion, not on signing the contract.
examples.zh: 款项在「竣工」时支付，而不是签合同时。

words.enDefinition: power to be effective; the quality of being able to bring about an effect

examples.en: The new rota's effectiveness shows in the shorter queue times.
examples.zh: 新排班表的「成效」体现在更短的排队时间上。

examples.en: We tested the glue's effectiveness on wet timber before ordering.
examples.zh: 下单之前，我们先在湿木料上测试了胶水的「效力」。

words.enDefinition: hypothesis that has been formed by speculating or conjecturing (usually with little hard evidence)

examples.en: Speculation in warehouse land pushed rents up before the bypass opened.
examples.zh: 绕城公路开通前，仓库用地的「投机」已把租金推高。

examples.en: Press speculation about a takeover unsettled the whole factory floor.
examples.zh: 媒体对「收购」的猜测让整个工厂车间人心浮动。

words.enDefinition: based in scientific and industrial progress

examples.en: Technological upgrades let the dairy track every churn by radio tag.
examples.zh: 「科技」升级让奶场能用射频标签追踪每一个奶桶。

examples.en: Old weavers remember when technological change emptied the mill towns.
examples.zh: 老织工还记得「技术」变革让磨坊城镇人去楼空的岁月。

words.enDefinition: restricting according to rules or principles

examples.en: The regulatory body inspects every fish market twice a year.
examples.zh: 「监管」机构每年对每个鱼市场检查两次。

examples.en: Regulatory approval for the new stone jetty took eighteen months.
examples.zh: 新石砌突堤的「审批」花了十八个月。

words.enDefinition: someone who enlists workers to join a union

examples.en: The organiser split the hundred stalls into eight numbered rows.
examples.zh: 「组织者」把一百个摊位分成八条编号的通道。

examples.en: As fair organiser, she books the stage and the security team.
examples.zh: 作为集市「主办方」，她负责预订舞台和安保团队。

words.enDefinition: a worker who takes part in a strike

examples.en: Each striker on the picket line took a turn holding the banner.
examples.zh: 纠察线上的每个「罢工者」轮流举着横幅。

examples.en: One striker read the company's offer aloud to the assembled crowd.
examples.zh: 一名「罢工者」向聚集的人群宣读了公司的方案。

words.enDefinition: voluntary gift (as of money or service or ideas) made to some worthwhile cause

examples.en: An anonymous donation of two hundred pounds repaired the school roof.
examples.zh: 一笔两百英镑的匿名「捐款」修好了校舍屋顶。

examples.en: The market's charity stall takes any donation for the lifeboats.
examples.zh: 集市慈善摊位接受任何金额的「捐赠」，用于救生艇基金。

words.enDefinition: failure to act with the prudence that a reasonable person would exercise under the same circumstances

examples.en: The court found negligence in leaving the loading gate unlocked overnight.
examples.zh: 法院认定，装卸门整夜未锁属于「疏忽」。

examples.en: His negligence with the gas rings nearly burned the kitchen down.
examples.zh: 他对燃气灶的「疏忽」差点把厨房烧掉。

words.enDefinition: tending to select; characterized by careful choice

examples.en: The wholesale club is selective about which producers it stocks.
examples.zh: 这家批发俱乐部对上架的生产商挑选得很「严格」。

examples.en: Selective cutting keeps the apple orchard healthy without heavy sprays.
examples.zh: 「有选择的」修剪让苹果园不用大量喷药也保持健康。

words.enDefinition: the act of making some area of land or water more profitable or productive or useful

examples.en: The mine's history includes the exploitation of generations of navvies.
examples.zh: 这座矿井的历史包含了对几代挖土工的「剥削」。

examples.en: Sensible exploitation of the peat bog funds the village school.
examples.zh: 对泥炭沼泽的合理「开发」支撑着村小学的运转。

words.enDefinition: legal proceeding in a court; a judicial contest to determine and enforce legal rights

examples.en: Costly litigation over the fence line dragged on for three years.
examples.zh: 围绕围栏界线的「诉讼」费用高昂，拖了三年。

examples.en: The insurer settled quickly to avoid litigation over the flooded stock.
examples.zh: 为避免水淹存货的「诉讼」，保险公司迅速和解。

words.enDefinition: making an important discovery

examples.en: A breakthrough in packaging kept the berries fresh for ten days.
examples.zh: 包装上的「突破」让浆果保鲜了十天。

examples.en: The young baker's breakthrough came with her seeded sourdough loaf.
examples.zh: 这位年轻面包师的「成名」靠的是她的籽料酸面团面包。

words.enDefinition: not made or become different

examples.en: Freight rates stayed unchanged through the whole of the spring season.
examples.zh: 整个春季，运费都保持「不变」。

examples.en: The recipe remains unchanged since the shop opened in 1962.
examples.zh: 自1962年开店以来，配方一直「未变」。

words.enDefinition: of or relating to or resembling a bureaucrat or bureaucracy

examples.en: Bureaucratic delays kept the export licence waiting for long months.
examples.zh: 「官僚」拖沓让出口许可证一压就是好几个月。

examples.en: Small traders complain about bureaucratic forms for every cattle move.
examples.zh: 小商贩抱怨每次转运牲口都要填「官样」表格。

words.enDefinition: formal confirmation that a person, product, or organisation meets specified requirements

examples.en: Organic certification for the creamery took two full growing seasons.
examples.zh: 奶油厂的「有机认证」花了整整两个生长季。

examples.en: Check the electrician's certification before he touches the fuse board.
examples.zh: 电工动手检修保险丝盒之前，先查验他的「资格证书」。

words.enDefinition: relating to or part of a binding legal agreement

examples.en: The haulier has no contractual duty to wait beyond thirty minutes.
examples.zh: 承运人「合同上」没有义务等候超过三十分钟。

examples.en: Their contractual right to the yard ends when the lease expires.
examples.zh: 租约到期，他们对场院的「合同」权利即告终止。

words.enDefinition: the act of enrolling

examples.en: Enrollment in the evening bookkeeping class doubled this autumn term.
examples.zh: 这个秋季学期，晚间簿记课的「报名人数」翻倍。

examples.en: Free enrollment attracted many dock workers to the safety course.
examples.zh: 免费「注册」吸引了码头工人来上安全课。

words.enDefinition: the state of being without a flaw or defect

examples.en: The baker's croissants are folded to perfection, layer upon layer.
examples.zh: 面包师的羊角包层层折叠，做得「完美」。

examples.en: Practice brought her icing work close to perfection by spring.
examples.zh: 到了春天，练习已让她的裱花近乎「完美」。

words.enDefinition: money set aside (as by a legislature) for a specific purpose

examples.en: The council's appropriation for harbour repairs passed without any debate.
examples.zh: 市政会港口修缮的「拨款」案未起争议便获通过。

examples.en: Next year's appropriation doubles the whole market square's maintenance budget.
examples.zh: 明年的「拨款」让市场广场维护预算翻倍。

words.enDefinition: a person who travels regularly between home and work

examples.en: The early ferry carries every commuter from the island before eight.
examples.zh: 早班轮渡八点前把岛上的每位「通勤者」送到对岸。

examples.en: Commuter parking by the station doubled the café's morning trade.
examples.zh: 车站旁的「通勤」停车让咖啡馆早市翻倍。

words.enDefinition: the act of pulling down or destroying a building or structure

examples.en: Demolition of the old grain silo begins after the nesting season.
examples.zh: 筑巢季一过，老谷仓筒仓就开始「拆除」。

examples.en: The demolition crew salvaged the slate before the walls came down.
examples.zh: 「拆除」队赶在墙倒之前抢救出了石板瓦。

words.enDefinition: an aggressive willingness to compete

examples.en: Cutting the turnaround time restored the port's competitiveness against Rotterdam.
examples.zh: 缩短周转时间重振了港口对鹿特丹的「竞争力」。

examples.en: The new subsidy shields farmers' competitiveness while input costs climb.
examples.zh: 投入成本攀升之际，补贴保护着农户的「竞争力」。

words.enDefinition: undisputed credibility

examples.en: The dealer guarantees the authenticity of every coin he sells.
examples.zh: 这位商人保证所售每枚钱币的「真实性」。

examples.en: Experts questioned the authenticity of the storm-damaged ledger's oldest pages.
examples.zh: 专家对那本遭风暴损毁账簿的「真伪」提出质疑。

words.enDefinition: state powerful enough to influence events throughout the world

examples.en: The grain deal linked a farming region with an industrial superpower.
examples.zh: 粮食交易把农业区和一个工业「超级大国」联系在一起。

examples.en: As an energy superpower, the state funds its own port upgrades.
examples.zh: 作为能源「超级大国」，该国自掏腰包升级港口。

words.enDefinition: section of a section; a part of a part; i.e., a part of something already divided

examples.en: Delivery terms appear in subsection four of the supply agreement.
examples.zh: 交货条款在供货协议第四「小节」。

examples.en: Check subsection (b) of the lease carefully before claiming the rebate.
examples.zh: 申领仓储返款前，先查看「分项」(b)。

words.enDefinition: having faults or defects; not working properly

examples.en: The faulty thermostat froze two whole crates of cream overnight.
examples.zh: 「失灵的」恒温器一夜之间冻坏了两箱奶油。

examples.en: We traced the billing errors to faulty software from the upgrade.
examples.zh: 账单出错的原因是升级带来的「有缺陷」软件。

words.enDefinition: the surrender of an insured interest to the insurer when claiming a total loss under marine insurance

examples.en: Notice of abandonment reached the insurers within the policy's deadline.
examples.zh: 「委付」通知在保单期限内送达了保险人。

examples.en: The abandonment of the flooded cargo ended the salvage attempt.
examples.zh: 「弃货」宣告了水淹货物的打捞努力结束。

words.enDefinition: the expertness characteristic of a professional person

examples.en: Her professionalism on the night of the fire impressed the inspectors.
examples.zh: 火灾当晚她表现出的「职业素养」令检查员印象深刻。

examples.en: Clients stay with the firm because of its quiet professionalism.
examples.zh: 客户留下来，靠的是公司低调的「专业精神」。

words.enDefinition: government building with five sides that serves as the headquarters of the United States Department of Defense

examples.en: The Pentagon announced new supply rules for all defence contractors.
examples.zh: 「五角大楼」宣布了对所有国防承包商的新供应规定。

examples.en: Reporters waited outside the Pentagon for the morning procurement briefing.
examples.zh: 记者们在「五角大楼」外等待采购简报。

words.enDefinition: consortium of independent organizations formed to limit competition by controlling the production and distribution of a product or service

examples.en: The freight cartel fixed haulage rates across the northern routes.
examples.zh: 货运「卡特尔」操纵了北部各条线路的运价。

examples.en: Cartel members share out the annual quotas at the spring meeting.
examples.zh: 「同业联盟」成员在春季会议上分配年度配额。

words.enDefinition: the act of conferring legality or sanction or formal warrant

examples.en: Customs authorization cleared the frozen lamb for the Sunday market.
examples.zh: 海关「许可」放行了周日市场的冷冻羊肉。

examples.en: Payment requires the written authorization of two signatories, not one.
examples.zh: 付款需要两名签署人的书面「授权」，一名不行。

words.enDefinition: remove the value from; deprive of its value

examples.en: The government moved to devalue the currency after the harvest failed.
examples.zh: 歉收之后，政府着手让货币「贬值」。

examples.en: Rising imports devalued the craft skills the village was proud of.
examples.zh: 进口货涌入让村里引以为豪的手艺「贬值」了。

words.enDefinition: belief in the importance of the individual and the virtue of self-reliance and personal independence

examples.en: The workshop prizes individualism, so each bench paints its own designs.
examples.zh: 作坊崇尚「个人主义」，每条工位都画自己的图案。

examples.en: His quiet individualism shows in the odd hours he keeps at the forge.
examples.zh: 他内敛的「个人主义」体现在铁匠铺里那些不寻常的作息上。

words.enDefinition: criminal offense of making false statements under oath

examples.en: The witness faced perjury charges after contradicting her own ledger.
examples.zh: 证人的说法与她自己账本矛盾，面临「伪证」指控。

examples.en: Lying under oath about the shipment dates amounts to perjury.
examples.zh: 就发货日期当庭撒谎即构成「伪证」。

words.enDefinition: forward movement

examples.en: The dredging crew finally made headway after the third week.
examples.zh: 第三周之后，疏浚队总算取得「进展」。

examples.en: We are making headway on the backlog of undelivered orders.
examples.zh: 未交付订单的积压问题正在逐步「解决」。

words.enDefinition: furnishing added support

examples.en: Wrapping and labelling are ancillary services charged by the hour.
examples.zh: 打包贴标属于「辅助」服务，按小时收费。

examples.en: The sawmill built an ancillary kiln to dry its own boards.
examples.zh: 锯木厂建了一座「附属」窑炉，烘干自产板材。

words.enDefinition: nonpayment of a debt when due

examples.en: The loan report flags any delinquency longer than ninety days.
examples.zh: 贷款报告会标记任何超过九十天的「拖欠」。

examples.en: Rising delinquency among the shop tenants worried the estate office.
examples.zh: 店铺租户「欠款」增多，让资产管理处担忧。

words.enDefinition: the development of industry on an extensive scale

examples.en: Industrialization moved the weaving from cottages into the new mills.
examples.zh: 「工业化」让织布从农家小屋搬进了新厂房。

examples.en: The railways drove industrialization faster than the old canals ever had.
examples.zh: 铁路推动「工业化」的速度远超旧日的运河。

words.enDefinition: run-down apartment house barely meeting minimal standards

examples.en: The whole family crowded into one room of the riverside tenement.
examples.zh: 全家挤在河畔「廉价公寓楼」的一个房间里。

examples.en: The council inspected the tenement stairwells before winter set in.
examples.zh: 入冬之前，市政会检查了这栋「旧公寓楼」的楼梯间。

words.enDefinition: the procedure of calculating; determining something by mathematical or logical methods

examples.en: The wage computation now runs automatically from the clock cards.
examples.zh: 工资「计算」如今由打卡记录自动完成。

examples.en: A slip in the duty computation cost the importer three hundred pounds.
examples.zh: 关税「计算」上的一处失误让进口商损失三百英镑。

words.enDefinition: misleading falsehood

examples.en: Selling the leaky barn as watertight is misrepresentation, plain and simple.
examples.zh: 把漏谷仓说成滴水不漏，纯属「虚假陈述」。

examples.en: The buyer sued the estate agent for misrepresentation over the inflated acreage.
examples.zh: 买方以面积夸大的「虚假陈述」为由起诉了房产中介。

words.enDefinition: (law) a gift of personal property by will

examples.en: A bequest of five hundred pounds funded the library's reading room.
examples.zh: 一笔五百英镑的「遗赠」资助了图书馆的阅览室。

examples.en: Her bequest left the workshop and its tools to the apprentices.
examples.zh: 她的「遗嘱」把作坊和工具留给了学徒们。

words.enDefinition: not having a job

examples.en: The jobless rate in the fishing quarter doubled last winter.
examples.zh: 去年冬天，渔业区的「失业率」翻了一番。

examples.en: Jobless yardsmen queued at the ferry office for mainland work.
examples.zh: 「失业的」船厂工人在轮渡办事处排队找对岸的活计。

words.enDefinition: rule of personal conduct

examples.en: The old trader's first precept was never to promise a price twice.
examples.zh: 老商人的第一条「准则」是从不二次承诺同一价格。

examples.en: Fair weighing is the market's founding precept, carved above the gate.
examples.zh: 公平称重是这个市场的立市「准则」，就刻在大门上方。

words.enDefinition: let off the hook

examples.en: The signed disclaimer does not absolve the carrier of care duties.
examples.zh: 签署的免责声明并不能「免除」承运人的照管义务。

examples.en: The tribunal absolved the driver because the fog was unforeseeable.
examples.zh: 因大雾无法预见，法庭「裁定司机无责」。

words.enDefinition: distribute anew

examples.en: The co-op votes to redistribute profits among its smallest members first.
examples.zh: 合作社投票决定把利润优先「再分配」给最小的成员。

examples.en: Surplus pallets were redistributed to the market gardeners at cost.
examples.zh: 富余托盘按成本价「调拨」给了市场菜农。

words.enDefinition: (law) an agreement or concession made by parties in a judicial proceeding (or by their attorneys) relating to the business before the court; must be in writing unless they are part of the court record

examples.en: The contract's main stipulation is delivery before the first frost.
examples.zh: 合同的主要「约定」是在初霜前交货。

examples.en: One stipulation forbids the subletting of stalls without written consent.
examples.zh: 其中一条「规定」禁止未经书面同意转租摊位。

words.enDefinition: sum of money allotted on a regular basis; usually for some specific purpose

examples.en: The apprentice receives a small stipend plus lodging above the bakery.
examples.zh: 学徒领取少量「津贴」，并住在面包店楼上。

examples.en: Her council stipend covers the ferry pass and work boots.
examples.zh: 她的议会「津贴」够付轮渡月票和工作靴。

words.enDefinition: judgment of not guilty

examples.en: The acquittal surprised everyone who had read the weighing records.
examples.zh: 看过称重记录的人都对这个「无罪判决」感到意外。

examples.en: After two hung juries, the third trial ended in acquittal.
examples.zh: 两次陪审团僵持后，第三次审判以「无罪开释」告终。

words.enDefinition: causing or able to cause nausea

examples.en: The crossing left several passengers queasy and leaning over the rail.
examples.zh: 这段航程让几位乘客一阵阵「恶心」，只好靠着船舷。

examples.en: He felt queasy about signing the deal without a survey.
examples.zh: 不做勘察就要签合同，他心里有点「发怵」。

words.enDefinition: the narrow part of a bottle near the top

examples.en: The single weighing bridge is the bottleneck at harvest time.
examples.zh: 收获季，唯一的过磅桥成了「瓶颈」。

examples.en: Hiring two more packers eased the packing bottleneck before Christmas.
examples.zh: 圣诞前多雇两名打包工缓解了「瓶颈」。

words.enDefinition: the conversion of wasteland into land suitable for use of habitation or cultivation

examples.en: Land reclamation added two acres to the quay for the timber yard.
examples.zh: 「填海造地」给码头增添了两英亩的木材场。

examples.en: Reclamation of the salt marsh took the villagers a decade.
examples.zh: 村民花了十年「开垦」那片盐沼。

words.enDefinition: habitual absence from work

examples.en: Monday absenteeism doubles whenever the ferry runs a late night.
examples.zh: 轮渡每开晚班，周一的「旷工」就会翻倍。

examples.en: The new bonus for full attendance cut absenteeism by half.
examples.zh: 新的全勤奖金让「缺勤」减少了一半。

words.enDefinition: seemingly boundless in amount, number, degree, or especially extent

examples.en: Her boundless energy kept the stall open through every storm.
examples.zh: 她「无穷的」精力让摊位在每场风暴里都照常营业。

examples.en: The apprentice showed boundless curiosity about every machine in the yard.
examples.zh: 学徒对货场里每台机器都怀着「无穷的」好奇。

words.enDefinition: (law) a voluntary repudiation of a person's legal claim to something

examples.en: Read the disclaimer on the ticket before boarding the hayride.
examples.zh: 乘干草车之前，先读一下票面上的「免责声明」。

examples.en: The catalogue carries a disclaimer about colour variations in yarns.
examples.zh: 目录里附有关于纱线色差的「免责声明」。

words.enDefinition: marked by abrupt transitions

examples.en: Trading turned choppy after the new fuel levy was announced.
examples.zh: 燃油附加费公布后，交易变得「震荡」。

examples.en: Choppy seas delayed the pilot boat by more than two hours.
examples.zh: 海面「波涛起伏」，引航船延迟了两小时。

words.enDefinition: relating to or involving money

examples.en: The judge awarded pecuniary damages for each of the lost contracts.
examples.zh: 法官就每一份丢失的合同判赔「金钱」损失。

examples.en: Pecuniary penalties apply to late filings at the trade registry.
examples.zh: 登记处对迟交的文件课以「金钱」处罚。

words.enDefinition: make unfashionable, outdated, or obsolete

examples.en: The outmoded card index finally gave way to a simple database.
examples.zh: 「过时的」卡片索引最终让位于简单的数据库。

examples.en: Buyers shunned the outmoded packaging style despite its fairer price.
examples.zh: 尽管价格公道，买家还是嫌弃那「老套的」包装。

words.enDefinition: deprive of status or authority

examples.en: The group was ordered to divest its stake in the ferry line.
examples.zh: 集团被要求「出售」其在轮渡公司的股份。

examples.en: The scandal finally divested the chairman of his trade honours.
examples.zh: 丑闻最终让这位主席被「剥夺」了贸易荣誉。

words.enDefinition: uninterrupted in time and indefinitely long continuing

examples.en: Three weeks of unremitting rain turned the market path to mud.
examples.zh: 「连绵不断的」三周降雨把赶集小道泡成了泥浆。

examples.en: Her unremitting care kept the orchard alive through the drought.
examples.zh: 她「不间断的」照料让果园熬过了旱季。

words.enDefinition: descriptive of any event or stimulus or process that has an effect on the effects of events or stimuli or process that occurred previously

examples.en: The retroactive pay rise covered every shift back to January.
examples.zh: 这次加薪「追溯」到一月份以来的每个班次。

examples.en: A retroactive tax on last year's exports angered the shippers.
examples.zh: 对去年出口「追溯」征税惹恼了货运商。

words.enDefinition: to give someone or something too much work, weight, or responsibility

examples.en: Don't overburden the night crew with day-shift repairs as well.
examples.zh: 别把白班的维修活也压给夜班，让他们「负担过重」。

examples.en: The old mule track was overburdened once the quarry reopened.
examples.zh: 采石场重开后，骡马道「不堪重负」。

words.enDefinition: someone who intrudes on the privacy or property of another without permission

examples.en: An interloper with cheap butter undercut every stall on the row.
examples.zh: 一个「闯入者」用廉价黄油把整排摊位的价都压了下去。

examples.en: The guild fined any interloper who sold within the walls.
examples.zh: 公会会对在城墙内兜售的任何「搅局的外来者」处以罚款。

words.enDefinition: declare invalid

examples.en: The judge moved to annul the lease signed by a minor.
examples.zh: 法官准备「废止」未成年人签署的租约。

examples.en: The registry annulled the merger papers because of missing signatures.
examples.zh: 因缺少签名，登记处「撤销」了合并文书。

words.enDefinition: full in all respects

examples.en: The plenary session votes on the harbour dues every autumn.
examples.zh: 「全体」会议每年秋季就港口税费表决。

examples.en: She holds plenary authority to sign contracts below ten thousand pounds.
examples.zh: 她拥有「完全」授权，可签署一万英镑以下的合同。

words.enDefinition: work produced by hand labor

examples.en: Her handicraft of rush baskets sells out by eleven most Saturdays.
examples.zh: 她的灯芯草篮子这种「手工艺品」多数周六十一点前就卖光。

examples.en: The museum shop stocks only local handicraft goods this season.
examples.zh: 博物馆商店本季只售卖本地「手工艺品」。

words.enDefinition: mass of precious metal

examples.en: The vault guards bullion shipments between the mint and the bank.
examples.zh: 金库护卫着铸币厂与银行之间的「金银锭」运输。

examples.en: Customs officers weighed all the bullion before sealing the strongbox.
examples.zh: 海关封箱之前称量了那些「金银块」。

words.enDefinition: a delay, or the amount by which something falls behind schedule

examples.en: Slippage in the delivery schedule pushed the fair back a week.
examples.zh: 交货计划的「延误」把集市推迟了一周。

examples.en: We allow one day's slippage between the ferry and the auction.
examples.zh: 轮渡与拍卖之间，我们预留了一天的「延误」余量。

words.enDefinition: not bound or pledged

examples.en: Two uncommitted growers still have not joined the export pool.
examples.zh: 还有两户「未表态的」种植户没有加入出口联营。

examples.en: Keep the van uncommitted until we know the festival dates.
examples.zh: 在确认节日档期之前，先别把货车「派定」用途。

words.enDefinition: to leave hurriedly and secretly, typically to avoid arrest or creditors, often taking money or property

examples.en: The cashier absconded with the weekend takings before the audit.
examples.zh: 审计之前，出纳带着周末的营业收入「潜逃」了。

examples.en: The tenant absconded owing two months' rent and the keys.
examples.zh: 租户欠下两个月房租，拿着钥匙「跑路」了。

words.enDefinition: revoke formally

examples.en: The new council voted to abrogate the old mooring rules.
examples.zh: 新市政会投票「废除」旧系泊规则。

examples.en: No partner may abrogate the pact without a year's notice.
examples.zh: 任何一方不得在不提前一年通知的情况下「废止」协议。

words.enDefinition: (usually followed by `to') able to be traced to

examples.en: Every crate is traceable back to the orchard by its stamp.
examples.zh: 凭印记，每只货箱都能「追溯」到来源果园。

examples.en: The missing payment was traceable to a mistyped account number.
examples.zh: 这笔失踪款项可以「追查」到一个误输的账号。

words.enDefinition: property inherited from one's ancestors; a heritage

examples.en: The orchard is the family patrimony, worked by four generations.
examples.zh: 这座果园是家族「祖产」，已传四代。

examples.en: Selling the patrimony to developers split the whole village council.
examples.zh: 把「祖业」卖给开发商让整个村委会分裂成两派。

words.enDefinition: appropriate (as property entrusted to one's care) fraudulently to one's own use

examples.en: The bookkeeper embezzled nearly nine thousand pounds from the petty cash.
examples.zh: 记账员「侵吞」了零用现金中近九千英镑。

examples.en: Anyone who embezzles club funds loses membership on the spot.
examples.zh: 任何人「贪污」俱乐部资金都会被当场除名。

words.enDefinition: wrongful conduct by a public official

examples.en: The report accused the harbourmaster of malfeasance over the mooring fees.
examples.zh: 报告指控港务长在系泊费上存在「渎职」行为。

examples.en: Council auditors uncovered malfeasance in two of the parking contracts.
examples.zh: 市政审计人员在两份停车合同中发现了「不法行为」。

words.enDefinition: divide society into social classes or castes

examples.en: The new seniority rules stratify the workforce into three pay bands.
examples.zh: 资历规则把员工「分层」为三个工资档。

examples.en: The new software stratifies the customers by their yearly spend.
examples.zh: 新软件按年度消费额对客户进行「分层」。

words.enDefinition: someone who travels about selling his wares (as on the streets or at carnivals)

examples.en: A hawker cried fresh mackerel along the quayside at dawn.
examples.zh: 清晨，「小贩」沿码头叫卖新鲜鲭鱼。

examples.en: All hawkers must display their market badge near the barrow.
examples.zh: 「叫卖小贩」须把集市徽章挂在推车附近。

words.enDefinition: official approval

examples.en: The new rota earned the approbation of every driver on shift.
examples.zh: 新排班表赢得了值班司机的交口「称赞」。

examples.en: Official approbation of the jetty design finally arrived in March.
examples.zh: 突堤设计的官方「认可」三月送达。

words.enDefinition: someone who travels about selling his wares (as on the streets or at carnivals)

examples.en: The pedlar called at the farm kitchens with ribbons and thread.
examples.zh: 「小贩」带着缎带和线团挨家敲开农舍厨房的门。

examples.en: A licensed pedlar may trade in the market before ten.
examples.zh: 持照「行商」可以在十点前进市场摆卖。

words.enDefinition: something that is lost or surrendered as a penalty;

examples.en: Forfeiture of the deposit followed the third missed delivery date.
examples.zh: 第三次误期交货后，定金被「没收」。

examples.en: The clause allows forfeiture of the stall licence for unpaid dues.
examples.zh: 条款允许对欠缴费用的摊位执照作「没收」处理。

words.enDefinition: someone legally empowered to witness signatures and certify a document's validity and to take depositions

examples.en: The notary stamped both paper copies of the partnership deed.
examples.zh: 「公证人」在合伙契约的两份纸质副本上盖了章。

examples.en: Bring your passport; the notary must verify every single signature.
examples.zh: 带上护照，「公证人」必须核实每一个签名。

words.enDefinition: only partly formed or developed; not yet complete

examples.en: Their claim to the old towpath remains inchoate until registration.
examples.zh: 登记完成之前，他们对旧纤道的权利主张尚属「初步」阶段。

examples.en: An inchoate idea for a night market filled his notebook.
examples.zh: 笔记本里记着他关于夜市的「初步」构想。

words.enDefinition: secure against future loss, damage, or liability; give security for

examples.en: The clause indemnifies the depot against claims from damaged freight.
examples.zh: 条款「保障」货场免受货损索赔。

examples.en: Insurers indemnify the stallholders for storm losses above the excess.
examples.zh: 保险公司对超过免赔额的风暴损失向摊主「赔付」。

words.enDefinition: an incidental benefit awarded for certain types of employment (especially if it is regarded as a right)

examples.en: A company flat is a perquisite of the depot manager's post.
examples.zh: 公司公寓是货场经理这个职位的一项「额外补贴」。

examples.en: Free boiler fuel was once a perquisite of the boilermen.
examples.zh: 免费的锅炉燃料曾是锅炉工的一项「特权待遇」。

words.enDefinition: the act of paying money

examples.en: The defrayment of the harbour dues took three counter visits.
examples.zh: 港口税费的「缴纳」跑了三趟柜台。

examples.en: Full defrayment of the repair bill satisfied the yard owner.
examples.zh: 维修账单的全部「付清」让场主放了心。

words.enDefinition: commission paid to a factor or agent for services

examples.en: The factor's factorage on wool sales is two and a half percent.
examples.zh: 代理商按羊毛销售额抽取百分之二点五的「代理佣金」。

examples.en: Factorage rises once the yearly sales pass the agreed threshold.
examples.zh: 年销售额超过约定线后，「代理佣金」随之上调。

words.enDefinition: capable of being corrupted

examples.en: The venal customs man waved the crates through for a note.
examples.zh: 那个「贪赃的」海关人员收了钱就放行货箱。

examples.en: Voters doubted the venal alderman's promises about the fish market.
examples.zh: 选民不相信那个「可以收买的」市政参事关于鱼市的承诺。
